If we determine that AI assistance was used by an applicant during an interview or an assessment, we reserve the right to immediately end the interview or assessment, disqualify the applicant’s candidacy and/or rescind any job offers extended.

Maven Securities is a leading proprietary trading firm that uses sophisticated technology and quantitative analysis to trade global financial markets. We specialise in options and derivatives market making, where your skills can have a real impact.

At Maven, we believe exceptional careers are built deliberately. Our summer internship is designed for a small number of high-potential students each year, combining structured training with practical exposure. We don’t hire large classes expecting only a few to succeed; we invest in every individual who joins the programme.

If you would like to be considered for our London Trader Summer Internship, applications will open on 7th September. We can only accept one application per candidate per recruitment cycle, so please ensure you apply to the role you are most interested in. 

Programme details

  • Location: Amsterdam
  • Programme dates: 21st June – 20th August 2027
  • Application deadline: Tuesday 20th October 2026
  • Key requirements: 
    • You must have the right to work in the region you are applying for at the time of application
    • You must be a penultimate-year undergraduate or master’s student
    • You must not have applied for any other Maven programmes in this cycle

Join a structured nine-week internship, giving you a practical introduction to options market making. The programme starts in our London office, with three weeks of interactive options theory classes led by one of our traders. You’ll then return to Amsterdam, quickly progressing into trading simulation and mock trading, helping you build the foundations you need to become a trader. You’ll also gain exposure to different desks through shadowing and project work.

Throughout the internship, you’ll be assessed on your performance and development. Successful interns may be considered for our Graduate Trader Programme the following year.

What you will be doing

  • Build practical trading skills in our simulation environment, applying your learning to real market scenarios
  • Use the same tools as our traders - or build your own - and observe the same trades being executed in the live market
  • Learn directly from traders across different desks through shadowing and regular interaction, with opportunities to ask questions and understand their day-to-day approach
  • Take part in a dedicated Reading Week, working independently on a project and exploring an area of interest

How and what you will learn

  • Build your foundations in options market making - we don’t expect prior knowledge
  • Develop your understanding of options theory, pricing, probability and risk with Maven’s in-house trainers
  • Apply your knowledge through trading simulation, testing different strategies, learning from experience and building confidence as a trader
  • Develop your understanding of the wider market through macroeconomics and technical training
  • Progress through clear learning milestones, with ongoing feedback from the Trading and Emerging Talent teams

Who you are

Key criteria

  • Strong numeracy skills and a good understanding of probability and statistics
  • A genuine interest in financial markets and a curiosity to learn
  • A willingness to adopt and utilise emerging AI technologies

We’re looking for someone who is

  • An entrepreneurial thinker who takes the initiative to generate ideas that further your learning and improve existing tools or systems
  • A critical problem solver and decision-maker who analyses situations and makes effective decisions
  • An agile learner who quickly acquires knowledge, responds to feedback and adapts to new situations
  • Able to synthesise information and turn complex or conflicting inputs into clear, actionable insights and decisions
  • Collaborative and influential, able to build trust, share what you have learned and work effectively with others
  • Results-focused and accountable, comfortable taking ownership and making decisions in the face of uncertainty and with incomplete information

Why Maven?

  • Dedicated in-house trainers: Learn through a programme designed for the Summer Trader Internship and delivered by Maven’s traders and in-house experts, covering technical and professional skills, as well as how AI is integrated into our daily work
  • Accelerate your career: Learn by trying new things, making mistakes and developing quickly. We’ve had traders progress to head-of-desk roles within two and a half years of joining as graduates. If you perform well and are ready, you can progress quickly
  • Proven pathways: Around a quarter of our workforce joined through an Emerging Talent Programme, including more than 50 of our current traders
  • Supported to succeed: Receive regular feedback, structured reviews and day-to-day support, including a Maven buddy
  • We invest in you: From the start of the internship, you’ll be immersed in a simulated trading environment and learn directly from traders. Throughout, you’ll gain practical insight into how our desks operate and have the opportunity to demonstrate your potential for the Graduate Trader Programme

 

Maven is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse workforce and inclusive environment. We welcome applications from all candidates regardless of background or identity.

 

Benefits at Maven

About the Role
BlackRock's Enterprise Data Platform (EDP) is the firm's strategic foundation for how data products are built, governed, and consumed at scale, powering investment decisions, risk analytics, and operational workflows across the firm and its global client base.

Data Platform as a Service (DPaaS) is a core capability within EDP, purpose-built to make data product creation fast, reliable, and repeatable. Whether a team is onboarding a new market data feed, publishing a risk dataset, or operationalizing a model output, DPaaS provides the infrastructure, tooling, and guided experience to take a raw data source and turn it into a trusted, production-grade data product. Teams get acquisition, ingestion, transformation, quality validation, and governance without having to build any of it themselves.

Why This Role is Exciting
Most engineers either build platforms or use them. As a Forward Deploy Engineer on the DPaaS team, you do both. You will deploy by embedding directly with teams across the firm, bringing their data products to life and solving real problems that only surface when a platform meets production data. You will build by developing solutions that fill gaps and make it easier for teams to create and publish data products on EDP. You will be at the frontier of how BlackRock thinks about data products, working with real users, influencing what gets built next, and seeing your work in production quickly across a wide range of data domains.

What You Will Do:

  • Forward Deployment & Data Product Onboarding
  • Embed directly with partner engineering and data teams to drive end-to-end data product onboarding onto DPaaS, from source configuration through to production
  • Work hands-on with teams to define data product structure including schema, ownership, SLAs, quality expectations, and governance attributes
  • Support onboarding of both structured and unstructured data products, adapting approaches to fit the nature of the data
  • Troubleshoot onboarding failures across infrastructure, pipeline, and data layers in real time
  • Run technical onboarding sessions and workshops tailored to each team's data product needs
  • Enable partner teams to self-serve on data product creation over time, reducing dependency on FDE support
  • Solution Development & Platform Contribution
  • Develop reusable data product accelerators including pipeline templates, configuration generators, and schema mapping utilities
  • Build custom acquisition connectors, ingestion templates, and transformation scaffolding for both structured and unstructured data
  • Contribute to core DPaaS platform engineering efforts including new feature development and framework improvements
  • Build and maintain data product accelerators and onboarding utilities that become reusable assets across the platform

  • Translate partner-specific data requirements into platform-compatible data product configurations
  • Document onboarding patterns, common failure modes, and solutions into reusable playbooks
  • Capture and channel structured feedback from onboarding engagements into the DPaaS product and engineering roadmap
  • AI Assisted Development & Intelligent Data Product Onboarding
  • Use AI assisted coding tools as a core part of daily workflow, accelerating configuration authoring, pipeline generation, and onboarding automation
  • Build and contribute to AI assisted onboarding workflows leveraging schema inference, automated attribute mapping, and AI driven data profiling to reduce manual effort
  • Implement emerging AI tooling including Model Context Protocol (MCP), AI agents, and Copilot extensions to automate repetitive onboarding tasks
  • Define what AI native data product creation looks like on EDP, contributing patterns that shape the platform roadmap

Account Managers represent PIMCO to our clients and prospective clients and seek to deliver investment solutions that leverage PIMCO’s position as one of the world’s premier fixed income investment managers.

Veterans Transition Program-Technical Relationship Manager, Aladdin – Associate

We recognize that veterans bring a unique and valued perspective to BlackRock thanks to their extraordinary backgrounds and experiences.  The Veterans Transition Program is designed to support veterans in making the transition from military life to the civilian workforce. The Program offers participants the opportunity to work at the world’s largest asset manager for six months. On completion of the Program, successful participants will be offered permanent employment at BlackRock.

Over the course of the Program, participants will:

  • Join teams and have an immediate impact;

  • Immerse themselves in the work of their teams;

  • Gain an understanding of how BlackRock serves its clients;

  • Be supported through training and mentorship;

  • Get exposure to senior leaders;

  • Participate in social and networking opportunities.

Program Structure:

The program begins with an orientation where you’ll learn about BlackRock’s principles, mission, purpose, and culture. You’ll learn about the asset management industry and get an in-depth look at how BlackRock serves its clients.  Following orientation, you’ll join your team and gain insights into the day-to-day life of an Associate as you develop subject-matter expertise through on-the-job learning and our industry-leading technology, Aladdin.

Aladdin® is an operating system for investment managers that seeks to connect the information, people, and technology needed to manage money in real time. The Aladdin platform combines risk analytics with portfolio management, trading, compliance, and operations tools on a single platform to power informed decision-making, effective risk management, efficient trading, and operational scale. Aladdin is used by a community of over 200 institutional clients around the world, including BlackRock. There are over 50,000 end users of Aladdin globally. The team is comprised of 800+ professionals responsible for implementing and supporting our Aladdin clients, sales and marketing, and ensuring the Aladdin Community maximizes Aladdin products through engagement and education.

We are seeking an Aladdin Technical Relationship Manager to work closely with Aladdin clients to be their trusted consultant, problem solver, and business partner – and to take full advantage of Aladdin.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Own relationships with client teams and help them use Aladdin to achieve their firm’s goals

  • Acts as a consultative partner to senior client stakeholders, providing product insights

  • Demonstrates strong segment and industry knowledge; accountable for multiple user segments / clients.

  • Apply deep client and technical expertise to shape regional themes and identifies risks and opportunities.

  • Ensure client feedback on product is communicated to the Product Managers and is tracked through successful development and deployment. 

  • Keep updated on regulatory and operational industry trends to help your clients stay ahead of changing times

About this role

Your team

The Aladdin Data Platform Engineering team builds and operates the foundational data and developer platforms that power the Aladdin ecosystem. Our portfolio includes the Enterprise Data Platform (EDP), Data Services and supporting infrastructure, and Aladdin Studio, the builder ecosystem for Aladdin.

Together, these platforms enable the Aladdin community to acquire, manage, govern, process, and distribute third-party and proprietary data at enterprise scale. Through Aladdin Studio, we provide the tools, services, and runtime capabilities that enable data producers, consumers, integrators, and application builders to create and operate solutions on top of Aladdin. We operate at significant scale across a complex global technology landscape, where reliability, performance, interoperability, security, and developer experience are critical.

Your role and impact

We are looking for an accomplished technical architect to help shape the future of Aladdin’s data platform. This is a senior individual-contributor leadership role for an architect who wants to do more than produce designs or provide technical advice. You will define architectural direction and work with engineering teams to turn that direction into production systems, common platforms, and measurable improvements in reliability, scalability, performance, and developer productivity.

Working across platform engineering, product, and operations, you will influence architecture across data platforms, application programming interfaces, shared services, and Aladdin Studio. You will combine deep technical expertise, strong engineering judgment, and the ability to simplify complex systems and drive decisions across a large engineering organization.

Your responsibilities

In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities:

  • Define and evolve the target-state architecture for Aladdin Data platforms, shared services, application programming interfaces (APIs), software development kits (SDKs), metadata, configuration, and data models, while guiding investments and technology adoption that improve scalability, reliability, performance, security, interoperability, and developer experience.

  • Shape platform capabilities for artificial intelligence (AI) and agent-based applications across structured and unstructured data, including metadata, retrieval, governance, application development, and workload orchestration.

  • Partner with engineering, product, and operations teams from technical discovery and prototyping through implementation, rollout, and adoption, validating architectural decisions against production outcomes and adjusting designs as needed.

  • Drive measurable improvements in availability, throughput, latency, scalability, onboarding speed, and engineering productivity, using recurring production and operational issues to identify and resolve systemic platform problems.

  • Define reference architectures, engineering patterns, and technical guardrails for code quality, testing, security, observability, resilience, and release management, and lead reviews that produce clear decisions while keeping governance practical and enabling.

  • Establish reusable, paved-road capabilities through libraries, templates, infrastructure, APIs, automation, tooling, documentation, and self-service patterns that reduce fragmentation and improve development speed and consistency.

  • Serve as a senior technical leader and force multiplier by mentoring engineers and architects, advancing modern engineering practices, and leading cross-platform initiatives that improve design quality, delivery automation, observability, resilience, and performance.

Your experience

  • Extensive experience in data platform architecture, data engineering, distributed systems, or related disciplines, including designing scalable, reliable, high-performance, and cost-effective enterprise data platforms across complex, multi-team environments.

  • Experience designing governed platforms for AI and unstructured-data workloads, including object storage, document management, metadata, retrieval, vector or graph technologies, security, and operational reliability.

  • Experience designing high-performance data services and APIs with demanding scale, availability, throughput, and latency requirements, supported by strong knowledge of distributed systems and integration patterns.

  • Technical fluency in data modeling and transformation, Structured Query Language (SQL), Python or Java, reusable packages, automated testing, and continuous integration and continuous delivery practices.

  • Experience with streaming and event-driven architectures using distributed event streaming and messaging platforms and stateful stream and batch data processing engines, including schema management, delivery semantics, event time, checkpointing, and fault tolerance.

  • Proven architecture leadership and technical judgment across workflow orchestration, Data Operations, release management, observability, cloud infrastructure, and source-control and delivery platforms, with the ability to simplify systems and make pragmatic trade-offs.

  • Ability to influence through technical credibility, align engineering, product, architecture, and executive stakeholders, communicate complex concepts clearly, and operate effectively in financial services or another highly regulated industry.

Role Summary

The product marketing director, ETF lead is a senior marketing leadership role responsible for leading product marketing efforts for ETFs across regions and business units. The role is accountable for shaping and creating relevant positioning, messaging, prioritization, and go-to-market direction in alignment with broader content and marketing strategies established across the organization within their remit. This role serves as the ETF subject matter expert for supporting teams across Product Marketing, Content & Insights (PMCI) , as well as partner teams across Investments, Global Product, Segment Marketing, and Distribution. Within their assigned remit, the product marketing director, ETF lead brings strategic perspective and investment expertise on asset classes, products, suites, and capabilities to help teams understand priorities, positioning, client needs, and commercial relevance.

The role combines strong investment acumen, product positioning expertise, and understanding of client need to shape differentiated value propositions, prioritize asset class-specific initiatives, and coordinate a cohesive content experience across channels and audiences.

The product marketing director, ETF lead acts as the “front door” for asset class/vehicle marketing priorities and intake, partnering closely with investment leaders, product managers, content strategists, editorial teams, segment marketing teams, and sales stakeholders to determine strategic importance and drive execution against business objectives.

Responsibilities

Asset Class / Vehicle Leadership:

  • Leads product marketing direction and prioritization for asset class, product suite, or capability aligned to business unit goals and enterprise marketing priorities.
  • Applies enterprise and content marketing strategies within the context of ETFs to ensure relevance, consistency, and commercial impact.
  • Where needed, serves as the primary coordination lead for asset class-related marketing opportunities, campaigns, and content requests.
  • Partners with content strategy, content creation, content enablement, segment, and client-facing stakeholders to align asset class priorities with broader organizational messaging, business objectives and market opportunities.
  • Recommends priority initiatives, sequencing, and resource allocation in partnership with leadership and cross-functional stakeholders within their asset class/vehicle.

Product Marketing Content & Positioning:

  • Develops differentiated value propositions, messaging frameworks, and positioning strategies for ETF capabilities and products.
  • Synthesizes complex market dynamics, client requirements, competitive intelligence, and industry trends to determine strategic product focus areas.
  • Identifies and incorporates into messaging the  competitive differentiators tailored to specific client segments, distribution channels, and regional markets.
  • Ensures consistency and alignment of messaging across campaigns, sales enablement materials, thought leadership, and client communications.
  • Advises on product focus priorities and strategic opportunities in partnership with Product Management and business leadership.

Client & Market Insight Leadership:

  • Maintains deep understanding of client needs, investment trends, and market developments impacting assigned asset classes.
  • Uses client insight, competitive analysis, and market intelligence to inform asset class marketing priorities and positioning recommendations.
  • Partners with business leaders and investment professionals to identify emerging client themes and opportunities for strategic engagement.
  • Integrates target audience insights into content strategy, content development, and client experience design.

Integrated Campaign & Content Leadership:

  • Leads integrated product marketing and communications planning for the assigned asset class across the client journey.
  • Drives alignment between asset class priorities and execution teams to ensure coordinated delivery of content.
  • Collaborates with Investments, Global Product,  content strategy, content creators and content enablement teams to prioritize – and when necessary, create – timely market insights, investment perspectives, and asset class content initiatives. While not the primary writer for asset class content, the role may directly create content when specialized expertise, strategic importance, or business urgency requires it. Provides strategic direction for custom content and collateral tailored to priority audiences and market segments.
  • Ensures campaigns and communications reflect business priorities, strategic messaging, and client-centric outcomes.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Influence:

  • Builds strong partnerships with Investment Heads, Portfolio Managers, Product Specialists, Product Managers, Distribution leaders, and Marketing stakeholders.
  • Influences senior stakeholders across business units to align on asset class priorities, positioning, and go-to-market execution.
  • Provides strategic recommendations and guidance to leadership regarding product development, commercialization, and market positioning.

Business Management & Performance Accountability:

  • Maintains ownership mindset for asset class or product suite business outcomes and marketing effectiveness.
  • In partnership with marketing intelligence, segment marketing and content strategists, helps establish explicit performance goals and success metrics for priority initiatives and campaigns. Report back to stakeholders on the performance of activity.
  • Monitors market response, campaign effectiveness, and business performance to refine strategies and optimize results.
  • Incorporates feedback, evolving market conditions, and business priorities into asset class planning and execution processes.

  • 10+ years of relevant experience in product marketing, investment marketing, asset management, product strategy, investment communications, or related disciplines.

Preferred:

  • Advanced degree and/or CFA designation preferred.
  • Deep understanding of investment products, asset classes, capital markets, and institutional/intermediary client segments.
  • Demonstrated experience developing positioning, messaging, and go-to-market approaches for complex investment capabilities.
  • Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and cross-functional leadership skills.

  • Experience leading integrated campaigns and collaborating across matrixed organizations.
  • Strong commercial orientation and understanding of business strategy, competitive dynamics, and client engagement.

Reporting to the APAC Financial Controller, this senior role will own financial control, statutory reporting and tax outcomes across Susquehanna’s Asia Pacific entities, spanning Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, India and China.

You will provide leadership to the broader APAC accounting team, act as a key point of contact for auditors, tax authorities and regulators across the region, and partner directly with trading desks and business leaders on budgeting, forecasting and financial performance.

 

This is an opportunity to take broad ownership across a genuinely multi-jurisdictional finance function while helping shape how the team, controls and processes evolve as the APAC business continues to scale.

 

Four Reasons to Join Susquehanna’s Team

  • Regional ownership: You will own the full financial control, statutory and tax outcomes for Susquehanna’s Asia Pacific entities across Australia, Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, India and China.
  • Leadership opportunity: You will lead, mentor and grow the APAC accounting team, playing a direct role in shaping the team’s development and structure as the region scales.
  • Senior stakeholder exposure: You will build senior relationships with stakeholders both onshore and offshore, including regional business leaders, auditors and global finance leadership.
  • Opportunity to shape the function: You will help drive the evolution of the APAC finance function through automation, stronger controls and continuous improvement across a complex multi-jurisdictional footprint.

What you’ll do

  • Own financial control, statutory reporting and tax outcomes across Susquehanna’s APAC entities.
  • Lead and develop the broader APAC accounting team, supporting capability development and effective delivery across the region.
  • Oversee statutory financial reporting and tax compliance requirements across multiple APAC jurisdictions.
  • Act as a key point of contact for external auditors, tax advisers, tax authorities and regulators.
  • Partner with trading desks and regional business leaders on budgeting, forecasting and financial performance.
  • Maintain effective financial controls and identify opportunities to strengthen processes, reporting and governance.
  • Lead complex, cross-border finance initiatives across multiple entities and time zones.
  • Drive automation and continuous improvement across finance systems, reporting tools and accounting processes.
  • Work closely with regional and global finance stakeholders to ensure local requirements are delivered within the broader finance framework.

What we're looking for

  • Degree and postgraduate professional qualification, such as CPA or CA, in a relevant field such as Finance or Accounting.
  • 10–15 years’ post-qualification experience, ideally gained across the APAC region, including demonstrated experience managing or leading a finance or accounting team.
  • Proven ownership of statutory financial reporting, tax compliance and external audit relationships across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Financial services experience is essential, for example within proprietary trading, banking, broker-dealer, asset management or a similar environment. Direct trading firm experience is advantageous.

  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills, with experience driving improvements to finance systems and reporting tools.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-border projects and manage competing deadlines across multiple entities and time zones.

 

What’s in it for you

  • Our flat hierarchy enables you to drive meaningful impact, by leveraging your expertise and taking ownership.
  • Private healthcare and gym allowances, plus wellness initiatives.
  • Additional leave entitlements including marriage leave and 2 bonus days annually.

  • Regular social, sporting and community events including annual poker tournament.
  • Matched donations and corporate discounts.

If you enjoy applying your quantitative and ML skills to real-world problems, coding production-quality analysis and tools, and working in a fast-paced environment with immediate and tangible feedback, our Summer Internship Program is ideal for you. 

At Brevan Howard, we build systematic and discretionary investment processes that rely on rigorous analysis of a vast universe of data, such as asset prices, macroeconomic indicators, news, sell-side research, and trading signals.

Transforming this data into actionable insights is central to how we win, and we’re looking to find the next generation of portfolio managers and quants through our internship program—people who are eager to push the frontier of research and engineering in global macro investing. 

Overview & Responsibilities 

You will work directly with our front-office personnel to provide immediate impact on a range of projects: 

  • Build pipelines to extract and analyze data, develop models and trading signals, and support decision-making of Portfolio Managers. 

  • Integrate AI into analytical systems as well as building new AI-powered tools using the latest LLMs and agent workflows. 

  • Contribute to our core analytics library, which is leveraged by Quants and PMs across the firm for research, trading and risk management. 

  • Our Internship Program starts with one-week in-depth training to prepare interns for the desk. This covers a range of topics relating to Financial Markets including Macroeconomics, FX, Digital Assets, Interest Rate Derivatives, Equity Rates, Bonds, Credit and Fixed Income, Trading Strategies, Risk Management, Excel and Python, and the latest AI tools and LLMs. 

  • Additionally, interns will benefit from key talks, a mentor program, social events and interactions with some of the most respected and talented individuals in their field. 

  • This internship is devised to provide candidates with an invaluable education on the workings of a multi-strategy hedge fund and the regulatory environment through a two-way process to determine if Brevan Howard and the intern are a compatible fit. 

  • The goal of our summer internship program is to convert top performing interns to our 2028 Graduate Program. 

Qualifications & Requirements 

  • A penultimate year undergraduate/junior or 1st year master's or PhD student at a recognized University — completed and awarded before July 2028. 

  • Strong mathematical, quantitative, problem-solving capabilities, and technical skills (Excel, VBA, R, AI and ML techniques). 

  • An interest and passion for financial markets, trading, and financial products. 

  • The ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team. 

  • An entrepreneurial spirit. 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. 

Why take this opportunity 

This is a unique opportunity to gain insight into one of the world’s leading firms operating at the forefront of macro trading. At Brevan Howard, we believe the future of investing lies at the intersection of deep domain expertise and cutting-edge technology. As our industry is being reshaped by AI and automation, you’ll see first-hand how LLMs, retrieval, and agent-like systems are being used in the front-office environment at one of the world’s premier macro hedge funds – where correctness, robustness and speed matter. 

Top-performing interns are considered for our Graduate Program the following year and longer-term paths include roles as analyst, quant, and portfolio manager. 

Please note that you may only submit one application to the Summer Internship Program globally. We encourage you to apply to the role and region that best align with your skills, experience, and interests.

Business - Private Wealth

Brookfield is one of the world's largest alternative asset managers, with a 100+ year heritage of owning and operating assets and businesses that from the backbone of the global economy. Through its broad platform, the firm offers investment strategies across real estate, infrastructure, renewable power and transition, private equity, and credit.

Brookfield's private wealth team extends these capabilities to intermediaries worldwide, partnering with financial advisors to provide institutional-quality investment opportunities and differentiated insights that support long-term objectives.

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

Job Purpose

Brookfield is seeking to add a lawyer to the BPW Legal and Regulatory Team, based in either its Hong Kong or Singapore office. Reporting to the Managing Director for Legal for BPW ex North America (who is based in London), the role will be primarily responsible for establishing local feeder funds, negotiating distribution agreements and other product distribution-related agreements with the wealth management intermediary channels and platforms in relation to Brookfield's private and registered funds as well as providing legal support to the BPW APAC team. The role will have responsibility for a range of work, including advising on the regulation, establishment, management, governance and marketing of Brookfield's investment funds within the wealth management channels. The investment funds in scope include closed end private funds, open end private funds, open end registered funds and evergreen registered funds and global feeder funds into the above funds. The candidate will collaborate with legal and regulatory personnel and teams across Brookfield and its affiliate managers, as needed, and engage with external counsel to ensure alignment of legal and regulatory approach(es) across Brookfield.

Key Competencies Required

  • Negotiate distribution agreements, letters of understanding, selling agreements and other product distribution-related agreements with the wealth management intermediary channels and platforms in relation to Brookfield's private fund and evergreen products.
  • Engage with Brookfield and its affiliates' internal and external legal counsel throughout negotiation of agreements with wealth management intermediaries.
  • Engage with personnel from technology platform partners that Brookfield contracts with to develop feeder fund structures for onshore and offshore distribution of products through wealth management intermediaries.
  • Advise the business on cross border sale of US and EU funds together with any offshore feeder funds into jurisdictions across APAC.
  • Assist in responding to due diligence queries from prospective investors specific to the legal structure of Brookfield funds.

Candidate Profile

  • Juris Doctorate (J.D) or equivalent from an accredited institution.
  • Licensed to practice law and a member in good standing in Singapore or Hong Kong (as appropriate).
  • 7+ years of experience, previous in-house experience preferred but will consider candidates from private practice with good experience with a focus on private funds and/or evergreen offerings and distribution-related matters.
  • Working knowledge of the rules and regulations impacting broker-dealers, onshore and offshore registered and private funds and evergreen offering, private fund structuring and formation, and feeder fund formation.
  • Working knowledge of, and experience working with and applying, the regulatory requirements and restrictions that apply to the marketing and distribution of private funds and evergreen offerings on a global basis.
  • Experience negotiating placement agent agreements, dealer agreements, platform/services agreements.
  • Familiarity with tax issues relating to private funds preferred but not required.
  • Strong client orientation with excellent interpersonal and communication skills, and ability to give commercial advice and guidance to internal clients.
  • Desire to work in a team‐based entrepreneurial environment with an ability to collaborate and build relationships with individuals at all levels of the organization.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills combined with attention to detail and thoroughness
  • Solid written and verbal communication.
  • Proficiency in Mandarin and/or Cantonese may be required to support engagement with clients, intermediaries and other stakeholders in Greater China where communications are conducted in those languages.
  • Resourceful, commercial and proactive when issues arise.
  • Able to establish priorities, work on multiple assignments, meet competing deadlines and work in a dynamic, fast-paced global environment.

Travel

Employee will need to be flexible and open to travel both domestic and international as needed.

About AQR Capital Management

AQR is a global investment management firm built at the intersection of financial theory and practical application. We strive to deliver superior, long-term results for our clients by seeking to filter out market noise to identify and isolate what matters most, and by developing ideas that stand up to rigorous testing. Underpinning this philosophy is an unrelenting commitment to excellence in technology — powering our insights and analysis. This unique combination has made us leaders in alternative and traditional strategies since 1998.

AQR takes a systematic, research-driven approach, applying quantitative tools to process fundamental information and manage risk. Our clients include institutional investors, such as pension funds, insurance companies, endowments, foundations and sovereign wealth funds, as well as financial advisors.

 

Technology is central to AQR’s success. As a Software Engineer in Portfolio Implementation, you will work on mission-critical systems that turn investment ideas into reality. Partnering closely with researchers and portfolio managers, you will design and build proprietary tools that support quantitative strategy research and systematic investing at scale.

Your Role :

As a Software Engineer in Portfolio Implementation, you will design, build, and extend systems that sit at the core of AQR’s investment process, including:

  • Portfolio Implementation platforms that consume research outputs, perform constrained optimizations, and generate orders
  • Cloud-based microservices engineered to run reliably and efficiently at scale
  • Participate in architectural design discussions for high-performance, high-volume, highly available systems, gaining experience with trade-offs across performance, flexibility, and maintainability
  • Bespoke technology solutions tailored to specific asset classes and evolving research needs
  • Collaboration with a global team of researchers, portfolio managers and engineers for successful product delivery

What You’ll Bring :

  • Degree in Computer Science or a related technical field
  • 2+ years of professional programming experience with strong proficiency in Java
  • Python experience is a strong plus, particularly for research integration and tooling
  • Strong software design skills and the ability to translate design concepts into high-quality, maintainable code
  • Excellent analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities
  • Clear and effective communication skills
  • Interest in financial markets and the investment process
  • Experience operating microservice-based architectures and building scalable, distributed systems, using technologies such as Java, Elasticsearch, Redis, RabbitMQ / AMQ, and relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MS SQL Server)
  • Strong engineering best practices, including attention to code quality, peer code reviews (PRs), automated testing, and test coverage
  • Experience operating, tuning, and profiling high-performance systems in production environments
  • Experience with observability and monitoring platforms (e.g., New Relic) is a strong plus

Who You Are :

  • Take strong ownership of your work, with the drive to see initiatives through from idea to completion
  • Comfortable leading change, overcoming obstacles, and navigating ambiguity to deliver results
  • Naturally collaborative, thoughtful, and effective in a team-oriented environment
  • Hard-working, curious, and eager to learn in a fast-paced setting
  • Committed to intellectual integrity, transparency, and openness

About the role 

Jump Trading Group is committed to world class research. We empower exceptional talents in Mathematics, Physics, and Computer Science to seek scientific boundaries, push through them, and apply cutting edge research to global financial markets. Our culture is unique. Constant innovation requires fearlessness, creativity, intellectual honesty, and a relentless competitive streak. We believe in winning together and unlocking unique individual talent by incenting collaboration and mutual respect. At Jump, research outcomes drive more than superior risk adjusted returns. We design, develop, and deploy technologies that change our world, fund start-ups across industries, and partner with leading global research organizations and universities to solve problems.

Our Data team is responsible for building a world class Data Platform with a centralized source of vendor and proprietary research data. This is a growing, high-visibility initiative, not greenfield, but early enough that this engineer will help shape it, with access across the entire platform as the team expands into proprietary datasets. The Vendor Data Group operates in a very dynamic environment utilizing a sophisticated and diverse technology stack, interfacing with all aspects of the firm (from Trading, Research, and Technology to Risk, Middle Office and Accounting) giving individuals within the group a full 360-degree view of Jump.

The Derived Data team, part of the Vendor Data Group, builds the analytical datasets that trading and research rely on: bars and residuals computed from market data, extending to curves, volatility surfaces, greeks, and other derived signals. As Jump's trading style has evolved, the team has brought in new alternative datasets. We are looking for a skilled Software Engineer that will help normalize that data and make it available to researchers and traders at massive scale.

What You’ll Do:

The ideal candidate will be able to dig into the technical details and work with end-users to understand their needs and implement streamlined solutions to deliver results. We are looking for individuals who are instinctively curious self-starters, demonstrating the ability to independently drive tasks and projects to completion in a team environment.
- Work with a variety of datasets, provide a scalable, centralized, validated representation of data for consumers to utilize.
- Review and understand various datasets leveraging vendor documentation, liaising with external vendors (many China-based) as needed to better understand data.
- Design, build, and maintain systems that calculate bars and residuals from market data, including streaming data captured in collocated environments.
- Extend the derived-data platform to additional analytics such as curves, volatility surfaces, and greeks.
- Work closely with trading and research teams to understand how they use derived analytics and deliver calculations that fit their workflows.
- Contribute to APAC production support, helping ensure continuity across the US–APAC time-zone handover.
- Document technical solutions and calculations clearly, translating complex methodology for less financially savvy stakeholders terms non-technical stakeholders can act on.
- Other duties as assigned or needed.

 Skills You'll Need:
- 5+ years of software engineering experience, with strong proficiency in Python. Rust or C++ is a strong plus. 
- 5+ years working on large sets of data and direct experience calculating bars and residuals from market data (ideally from streaming, collocated market data).
- Good understanding of trading and research, and how trading teams work with analytical research.
- Strong unit-testing / test-driven coding style.
- Experience working with various data storage formats, filesystems, and event queues preferred.
- Hands-on experience working within a Linux environment.
- Preferred working proficiency in Mandarin to collaborate with the Shanghai-based team and liaise with China-based vendors.
- Willingness to diversify and master other technical skills on the job.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to document technical solutions and calculations in non-technical terms.
- Reliable and predictable availability.

About Bridgewater 
Bridgewater Associates is a premier asset management firm, focused on delivering unique return streams, insight and partnership for the most sophisticated global institutional investors. 
Our investment process is driven by a tireless pursuit to understand how the world’s markets and economies work — using cutting-edge technology to validate and execute on timeless and universal investment principles. 
Founded in 1975, we are a community of independent thinkers who share a commitment for excellence. By fostering a culture of openness, transparency, and inclusion, we strive to unlock the most complex questions in investment strategy, management, and corporate culture. 
Explore more information about Bridgewater on our website here. 
Our Culture 
Our culture is anchored in excellence, meaning constant improvement, and it is deeply tied to our mission. Because markets are objective, competitive, and getting smarter everyday, we need to keep rapidly improving to have any chance of beating them. Truth is our most essential tool for engaging with the markets and constantly improving because once you know what’s true about your problems and opportunities, you can determine how to get better. Valuing truth means being transparent about your decision-making and mistakes, giving and receiving feedback with humility, and fighting for the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest. Operating this way is hard – it’s only possible because we build meaning in our work and relationships. This meaning comes from the audacity of the mission, and the joy of working alongside people who make you a better version of yourself. The culture, like Bridgewater itself, is always evolving. In 1997 our founder Ray Dalio wrote down his lessons, starting with a Philosophy Statement which remains our foundation. This later evolved into a set of 300+ Principles. In 2022, when Ray transitioned the company, we re-underwrote several of those principles and evolved others, with a specific focus on Meritocracy. Today the culture sits, alongside our people, as our most important edge. When we get it right, it’s the engine that powers everything else. 
Explore more information about Bridgewater’s culture on our website here. 
About Your Role 
Bridgewater’s mission has always been to understand how the world works and translate that understanding into the best possible portfolios for our clients. The Client Investment Research Analyst role sits at the center of that translation. It is a role unlike others in asset management: you take Bridgewater’s view of the cause-and-effect linkages in economies and markets and put it to work advising the world’s most sophisticated institutional investors.  
You will work on the investment problems facing Bridgewater’s institutional clients: sovereign wealth funds, large public pensions, endowments, and other major allocators. The work spans the full range of what these institutions need from a macro investment partner, from synthesizing what’s going on in the world, to considering how to best manage a portfolio from the perspective of each investors’ unique goals and constraints, both strategically and tactically. You will do this alongside Bridgewater’s Strategists, a small group of senior investors appointed by our co-CIOs to lead our work with allocators; as you develop, you will take on more of the investment content those engagements carry. 
What the role builds. Over time, you develop what we call proxy CIO judgment: the ability to stand in an institutional investor’s shoes, understand their full set of constraints and objectives, and form a view on how to manage their portfolio both strategically and in view of the macro environment today. You apply Bridgewater’s macro thinking to institutional portfolios and the constraints they operate within. You also develop a working understanding of how large allocators make decisions: their governance, return objectives, liability profiles, and strategic priorities. 
Growth and career paths. Analysts progress from building foundational skills through to independent investment practitioner and, for those who continue on the team, into senior leadership roles where they operate as close partners to Strategists. At the senior end, you will hold a view on Bridgewater’s synthesis of the macro environment and portfolio construction, as well as which investment content will most change how our clients think about their portfolios. The capabilities you build here open many paths across Bridgewater’s investment community over time. The specific path depends on your strengths, interests, and how your capabilities develop. 
Day-to-day responsibilities include: 

Designing analytical approaches to complex investment questions and executing the research from framing through synthesis 
Partnering with Strategists, co-CIOs, and asset class research teams to develop investment content for client engagements 
Synthesizing Bridgewater’s macro outlook and translating it into investment narratives tailored to each institution’s context 
Developing independent views on markets, institutional asset allocation, and the macro environment to inform our work  
At senior levels: developing junior analysts, setting team quality standards, and contributing to broader investment research priorities 

Interested in learning more about working at Bridgewater? Hear about the experiences of our employees here. 
About the Departments

Alpha Engine: The Alpha Engine is responsible for Pure Alpha, Bridgewater’s flagship alpha strategy launched in 1991. Our aim in Pure Alpha is to generate high and consistent returns, uncorrelated to markets and other managers over time. We pursue this by systematically deploying our fundamental understanding of markets and economies to trade long, short, and relative value across roughly 200 liquid public markets. 
Client Investment Research within the Alpha Engine partners deeply with Pure Alpha clients and prospects on their highest-priority investment questions. We share our understanding of key dynamics driving markets and economies and advise on navigating the current market environment as well as more timeless investment challenges. Analysts also help shape how we communicate our Pure Alpha investment philosophy and process, alongside our performance and positioning amid evolving market conditions. 

AIA: What's happening in AI will likely amount to some of the most consequential technological and societal changes in modern history, and it's increasingly clear that everyone will need a plan for how to navigate them. At Bridgewater, we approach AI from two angles: as investors working to fully capture how AI is reshaping markets and economies, and as practitioners pushing the limits of what AI can do to transform how we manage money. Our central effort as practitioners is building AIA, a fully functional artificial investor designed to meet or exceed human performance across the full range of activities a human investor performs: forming views on markets, sizing positions, and revising them as conditions change. Building on the capabilities and expertise developed along the way, we are also using AI to transform our human-driven process in Pure Alpha. 
Client Investment Research within AIA partners deeply with clients and prospects on how AI is reshaping markets, economies, and their portfolios. We share our understanding as both investors and practitioners: what we see in the data and what we are learning from building a fully functional artificial investor ourselves. We advise on navigating AI's implications, from exposures across markets to the broader macro environment. Analysts also help shape how we communicate Bridgewater's investment thinking on AI, our approach to managing money with it, and the lessons we are drawing as practitioners. 
Strategic Investment Engine (SIE): SIE is responsible for Bridgewater’s strategic investment management, managing over $30B in long-asset strategies for many of the world’s largest and most sophisticated institutions. Our aim is to help investors achieve their long-term investment goals for compounding wealth by balancing relative and absolute return objectives. SIE deploys the same fundamental, systematic investment process that underpins all of Bridgewater’s investment strategies, applied to the particular challenge of being the ‘Best Long-Term Investor’.  
Client Investment Research Associates within SIE partners deeply with Bridgewater clients and prospects on their strategic investment questions. We share our understanding of key dynamics driving portfolio outcomes and advise on ways that clients can maximize the likelihood of achieving their goals given their circumstances. Analysts also help shape how we communicate Bridgewater’s investment philosophy and process, alongside our performance and positioning amid evolving market conditions. 
Asia: The goal of the Asia Strategies team is to create industry-leading portfolios and investment thinking in Asia, helping investors navigate the changing geopolitical and macroeconomic paradigm. This entails growing deep regional expertise, generating alpha in Asian markets, researching and publishing our understanding of the macroeconomic environment, and designing portfolio solutions to help our clients invest across the region.  
Bridgewater has a long history as an asset manager in Asia. It started when our founder, Ray Dalio, first visited China in 1984, and we have been trading Asian markets since 1992. Asian markets have always been a core part of our global macro investment strategies, and Asian economies feature prominently in the research we have published on debt cycles and the changing world order. Bridgewater has offices in only two places – the US and Asia – reflecting the region’s strategic importance. Our first Asia-focused fund, launched in 2018, is now among the largest private funds in China. 
Position Requirements 
This role is designed for candidates who want to develop as investment practitioners. Deep asset management experience is not required at entry, but you should arrive with a genuine passion for markets and investing, as well as the analytical foundation for rigorous investment work.  
Minimum Qualifications 

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree with a strong academic and extracurricular track record 
Demonstrated interest in and understanding of markets and investing; you should have views, not just awareness 
Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, well-structured investment narratives 
Creativity and strong problem-solving instincts, including the analytical and quantitative capability to work with financial and economic data

To succeed within Bridgewater’s culture, individuals must demonstrate humility, innate curiosity, and openness to new ideas. Candidates must be driven, confident, and oriented toward self-improvement through direct feedback and honest self-reflection.   • Identify opportunities to improve workflows, reporting, analytics, and automation to enhance the efficiency and scalability of the Equity Capital Markets function.

The Senior Analyst, Private Equity Operations, will be responsible for executing and managing operational activities across the private investment lifecycle, including deal approval, execution and settlement, IPOs, restriction tracking, corporate actions, and liquidity events. The Senior Analyst will coordinate across functional teams when material events occur and oversee private placement vendors and other outsourced functions.

  • Review and resolve discrepancies on reconciliation reports - cash/position/security master – to ensure the investment book of record is in good order daily

  • Review GP’s reporting, including capital account statements and financial statements, and reconcile commitments, contributions, distributions, unfunded commitments, NAV, ownership interests, fees, and other activity to Wellington’s books and records

  • Investigate and resolve discrepancies with GPs, fund administrators, and internal teams; interpret relevant fund terms; and ensure material lifecycle events are accurately reflected across accounting, valuation, performance, and reporting processes. Oversee the third-party vendors and related processes that support these activities

  • Adapt and evolve processes, controls, workflows, and systems to support new private funds and new asset classes   

  • Ensure stakeholders receive consistent, timely and accurate communication for operational events associated with private placements

  • Support data needs for all functional teams involved in the private process, in particular, for performance and internal/LP reporting

Your team 

At the core of BlackRock’s global operations, the Technology & Operations team enables the firm to scale, innovate, and deliver for clients. Within Technology & Operations, the Outsourced Platform Services (OPS) team leads the design and deployment of middle and back office operating models and solutions that support our outsourced service model on BlackRock’s proprietary investment platform, Aladdin. 

As a member of OPS, you will work directly with clients and internal partners to shape how investment accounting functions are designed and executed. The team translates business needs into scalable, resilient processes and operating models that support complex investment strategies across multiple asset classes. You will collaborate across functions to implement solutions that are aligned with BlackRock’s technology ecosystem and client service model. 

Your role and impact 

As an Investment Accounting Implementation Director, you will lead strategic client transformations involving investment accounting operating models, accounting books of record, and platform implementations. You will be responsible for the successful delivery of complex, large-scale implementation programs while partnering across Accounting, Investment Operations, Technology, Product, and Client businesses. 

You will serve as a senior client advisor and implementation leader, providing strategic direction throughout the implementation lifecycle. Through your investment accounting expertise, leadership capabilities, and focus on operational excellence, you will help clients modernize operating models, mitigate risk, and realize the full value of BlackRock’s outsourced operating model and Aladdin platform. 

Your responsibilities 

  • In every role at BlackRock, you'll be expected to apply sound judgement and critical thinking to solve complex problems, adapt as the business evolves, and combine the curiosity to explore new approaches and technologies with the rigor to challenge the results. The scope of this role also includes the following responsibilities: 

  • Lead large-scale accounting transformations bringing the investment accounting book of record onto Aladdin and implementing operating model change across asset classes and investment strategies. 

  • Serve as the senior implementation lead for complex client engagements, providing strategic oversight throughout planning, execution, and post-implementation stabilization. 

  • Partner with clients and stakeholders to design scalable investment accounting operating models that align with business objectives and industry best practices. 

  • Drive governance, implementation methodology, project execution, and delivery excellence across multiple concurrent programs. 

  • Develop deep subject matter expertise in investment accounting processes, operating models, and platform capabilities while helping shape strategic enhancements to implementation offerings. 

  • Identify implementation and operational risks, establish mitigation plans, and provide executive-level reporting to stakeholders and leadership. 

  • Partner closely with Technology, Product, Accounting, and Operations teams to influence platform capabilities and improve client outcomes. 

  • Mentor and develop implementation professionals while building organizational capability and implementation expertise across the team. 

  • Build strategic partnerships with Technology, Product, and Operations leadership to shape and promote the adoption of AI-enabled Aladdin functionalities across implementation programs, while driving a culture of innovation that aligns AI tooling with BlackRock’s strategy, implementation standards, and client delivery objectives. 

  • Contribute to strategic initiatives that improve scalability, operational effectiveness, risk management, and implementation efficiency. 

Your experience 

  • Understanding of investment management and investment accounting, supported by seven or more years of relevant industry experience. 

  • Significant experience in investment accounting, accounting platforms, accounting operating models, client implementations, or related transformation programs. 

  • Proven track record of leading large-scale transformation projects, including operating model implementations, platform migrations, accounting conversions, and process transformation initiatives. 

  • Strong knowledge of accounting principles, investment accounting workflows, accounting books of record, and operational processes supporting institutional investment managers. 

  • Demonstrated experience leading complex programs involving multiple stakeholder groups and cross-functional teams. 

  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and executive client audiences. 

  • Strong numerical, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to leverage data in support of strategic decision-making. 

  • Ability to organize and manage multiple priorities while maintaining a strategic, collaborative, and execution-focused approach. 

  • Experience developing talent, leading teams, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. 

  • Curiosity and an interest in learning about financial markets, accounting processes, data, and emerging technology.

About the Role: 

Aladdin Studio represents the next generation of extensibility within the Aladdin platform. It enables clients to build, integrate, and customize workflows, applications, and data pipelines on top of Aladdin—supporting scalable innovation across data, APIs, analytics, and user experiences. 

Aladdin Studio is designed for both technical and non-technical users, empowering developers, data engineers, product teams, and business users to create differentiated capabilities while maintaining enterprise-grade governance, performance, and security. 

As a Product Marketing Lead for Aladdin Studio, you will sit at the center of product, engineering, and go-to-market—acting as the strategic marketing lead embedded within the Studio ecosystem. This role is positioned as a senior individual contributor / lead PMM, owning how Aladdin Studio is brought to market and adopted globally. 

You will operate as the primary marketing partner to Studio Product, ensuring tight integration between product development and market execution. You will shape the narrative for a highly technical platform while driving clarity, relevance, and measurable business outcomes for both technical and non-technical audiences. 

This role requires deep comfort engaging with technical concepts (APIs, data workflows, platform architecture, AI capabilities) while consistently elevating those concepts into compelling, outcome-driven narratives for clients and internal stakeholders.  You will also play a leadership role in scaling product marketing impact, influencing cross-functional priorities, and setting the standard for how platform capabilities are marketed across Aladdin Studio.

Product Positioning & Market Strategy

About Aladdin Engineering

Aladdin is BlackRock’s end-to-end investment management and operations platform — trusted by hundreds of institutional clients and advisors globally, supporting over $21 trillion in assets across the investment lifecycle.

The Aladdin Engineering Group designs and scales technology for tomorrow’s challenges. We build innovative solutions that serve both BlackRock and our global client ecosystem — operating at the speed of a startup with the reach and resources of the world’s largest asset manager. Our engineers take emotional ownership of what they build, shipping products that clients rely on every day.

About ETF Systems

The ETF Systems Engineering team builds the technology powering BlackRock’s iShares primary markets business — the world’s largest ETF franchise. The team owns the ETF Servicing Platform (ESP), a multi-tenant platform at the heart of the ETF ecosystem, enabling ETF Issuers, Authorized Participants, and Service Providers to meet and grow demand for the ETFs they manage, custody, or make markets in.

The engineering organization also owns a suite of mission-critical applications including Basket Management, Order Capture, Order Fulfillment and Custom Basket Negotiation serving clients from ETF Capital Markets, Portfolio Management and Operations across the globe.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Head of Engineering to lead the ETF Systems engineering organization — a globally distributed team of 50+ engineers across San Francisco, New York, Atlanta, London, and Singapore.

This is a senior leadership role accountable for the technical vision, delivery execution, operational excellence, talent strategy, and AI transformation of a platform that underpins one of the fastest-growing segments of the global asset management industry. You will partner closely with Product Management, iShares business leadership, and Aladdin platform teams to scale systems that support new market expansion, new asset classes, and platform commercialization.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise with strong organizational leadership — someone who takes emotional ownership of outcomes, inspires engineering excellence, and thrives in a fast-paced, high-accountability environment.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership & Architecture

  • Define and drive the long-term technical vision for the ETF engineering platform, ensuring alignment with Aladdin-wide architecture standards and BlackRock’s technology strategy.
  • Own domain architecture decisions across ESP and adjacent systems — including microservices decomposition, event-driven architectures (Kafka), cloud-native infrastructure, and API design.
  • Lead the resiliency strategy for ETF critical workflows (Creation/Redemption), including high availability, isolation, and graceful degradation across application and platform layers.
  • Establish and enforce engineering standards for code quality, observability, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and release governance.

AI Strategy & Adoption

  • Define and execute the AI/GenAI adoption strategy for ETF Engineering — identifying high-value opportunities for AI-assisted development, intelligent automation, and AI-powered product features.

  • Establish governance frameworks for responsible AI use — including model risk management, data governance, and compliance with BlackRock’s AI principles.
  • Partner with Aladdin AI/ML platform teams and vendor partners to evaluate, pilot, and scale AI capabilities across the ETF technology stack.

Delivery & Execution

  • Oversee delivery across multiple product engineering teams operating in an Agile/SAFe framework.
  • Drive release governance and software change management processes in partnership with Product Management and business stakeholders.
  • Manage cross-team dependencies with Aladdin platform teams and external integrations (DTCC/Fund/SERV, custodians, liquidity providers).

The Market Data team designs and operates the high-performance systems that power our production trading environment. In our business, market data correctness, determinism, throughput, and latency directly impact trading performance and P&L.

Strong debugging and problem-solving skills in complex, real-time production environments.

Job Description

Role Overview:

The team
Citadel Securities is one of the largest market makers in the world, providing liquidity across nearly every major asset class and market globally, in real time. Machine learning is fundamental to how we do it.

We are the firm’s centralized applied-AI team, working with strategy teams across the firm. We conduct the frontier model research that benefits all of them in common — the deep-learning models that predict where prices are going — and we tailor that research to the highest-impact strategies. We build the systems that turn those predictions into trading decisions, as well as the tooling that enables researchers across the firm to apply machine learning to their own problems. As the centralized team, we take on the hardest applied-AI problems first and set the standard the wider organization follows. Our research is applied: it ships to production and is measured by its impact on the business.

Every member of the team is a member of technical staff — a strong generalist with depth in at least one specialty, whether deep learning, large-scale ML systems, applied LLMs and agents, or the mechanics of markets themselves. We operate in small teams with end-to-end ownership and minimal bureaucracy.

The role
You build ML applications and systems that move real money, and you want to understand why they work — not simply ship them. You write code once you understand the research context and why it matters, and you are equally comfortable reading a research paper and profiling a training run.

As Quantitative AI Technical Staff, you will have substantial independence to pursue the research directions you believe are most impactful, supported by state-of-the-art clusters with a very high compute-to-researcher ratio and by dedicated engineering, hardware, and systems teams that help bring your ideas into production. You will be responsible for improving every part of our models — from how we featurize raw market data, to architecture design, to training dynamics, to how a model’s predictions become trading decisions. The role is approximately half research and half engineering.

Your work will be directly and measurably impactful on the business, and it will be challenging: this is a field with no easy or obvious solutions.
Prior experience in finance or markets is not required. Many of us joined without it; we hire for ability, curiosity, and growth trajectory, and we will teach you the markets. This is an entry-level role, and we welcome candidates whose qualifications align with the position.

How we work
We work in an AI-native way. Directing several coding agents in parallel — to run experiment sweeps, refactor subsystems, or investigate issues across a large codebase — is a normal part of the workflow, and we expect everyone to develop fluency in it.

We hold ourselves to a high standard of scientific rigor. Because our results translate directly into capital at risk, sound research methodology is essential: forming clear, testable hypotheses; designing controlled and reproducible experiments; comparing approaches on a consistent, like-for-like basis; and carefully distinguishing genuine signal from noise or overfitting. We value researchers who are skeptical of their own results and who validate their conclusions before acting on them.

The systems we work with are complex, and understanding them well is part of the job. Clear communication matters: we collaborate continuously with quantitative researchers and traders across a large organization.

Responsibilities:

Model research. Design and train the deep-learning models that predict where prices are going — developing new architectures, improving features, and extending how far into the future the models can reliably predict.
Enabling ML across the firm. Build the systems and tooling that allow many other researchers to apply machine learning to their own problems, multiplying your impact well beyond your own work.
High-impact markets. Take on novel problems in markets that generate billions of dollars in annual revenue, where established solutions do not yet exist.
From prediction to trading decisions. A prediction is only useful once it informs a decision to buy or sell. We apply AI across the full chain — including simulating how a set of trades would perform before any capital is committed, and a growing range of decision problems beyond prediction itself.

What makes it challenging
The problems are difficult and genuinely adversarial: predicting price movements from the fine-grained patterns in how millions of orders arrive and change, extending those predictions further into the future, simulating trading outcomes accurately, and building infrastructure that supports many distinct trading strategies at once. Unlike most AI work, which is evaluated on benchmarks, our work is evaluated by the market — a demanding, high-stakes environment with immediate feedback. The quality of your work is reflected directly and quickly in measurable financial outcomes.

Qualifications:

Have strong software engineering fundamentals and write clean, efficient, correct code.
Have solid depth in machine learning and deep learning, with hands-on experience training and debugging models.
Are results-oriented, with a bias toward action, flexibility, and efficiency.
Are genuinely curious about how markets work and why trades are profitable, even without a prior finance background.
Communicate clearly and collaborate effectively across a large, technical organization (this role involves substantial collaboration).
Are coachable and respond well to feedback; we value growth trajectory over starting point.
Are comfortable working in an AI-native way, directing multiple agents to carry out research and engineering, or are eager to learn.

Strong candidates may also have experience with
(None of the following is required, but any of it is a real plus.)

Building applications with LLM agents (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, or custom frameworks) at meaningful scale.
Transformer architectures and modern foundation models; post-training techniques such as supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or preference optimization.
High-performance or large-scale ML systems; GPUs/TPUs; JAX or PyTorch.
Large-scale data pipelines and distributed training.
A demonstrated record of excellence in a demanding area — for example, competitive programming, mathematics or physics olympiads, Kaggle, significant open-source contributions, or research publications.

Basics

Education: Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD — or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience — in a relevant field (computer science, mathematics, physics, electrical engineering, statistics, or similar).
Experience: Entry-level; graduates across all degree levels are encouraged to apply. Required experience will correspond to the internal level of the position.

About Us

Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.

About the Role

THE POSITION

This role sits within the firm’s Enterprise Strategy Office, which reports into the CEO, and is primarily aligned with the Firm & Product Strategy function. Firm & Product Strategy is responsible for the firm’s enterprise strategy framework and manages processes to oversee product prioritization and product development firmwide. In addition, the function serves as the firm’s center of excellence for market intelligence and product innovation.

The Director of EMEA Strategy will partner with Wellington’s leaders, and engage key distribution partners, to shape strategy and drive growth. The Director will focus on driving end-to-end development of new products. In addition, they will serve as a thought partner to regional leaders, conduct research to help leaders “think around corners,” lead key strategic projects, inform resource allocation decisions and contribute to enterprise strategy processes. The role will focus predominantly, but not exclusively, on wealth and maintain a dotted line relationship with the Head of EMEA Wealth to foster close connectivity with the business.

Executing these responsibilities will require The Director to maintain a broad base of industry, product, vehicle and regulatory knowledge. The Director will partner with business developers to selectively build and maintain relationships with key clients, distribution partners and wealth technology platforms to help uncover commercial opportunities and support market-led product development.

Key responsibilities of the role include:

  • Drive end-to-end product development. This work will involve orchestrating cross-functional teams (e.g. Legal, Compliance, Tax, Operations, Investments, Distribution) to drive disciplined, on-time execution from concept through launch and commercialization.

  • Lead a range of complex strategic projects for senior Wellington leaders.

  • Working with line management in the region, build business case for locally relevant investment strategies as an important element of the building of the EMEA Strategy. The ability to partner with the EMEA Management Team to ensure alignment and support is critical in this regard.
