About the position

We are looking for Quantitative Researchers to help us build models, strategies, and systems that price and trade financial instruments. You’ll work side by side with experienced researchers who are committed to teaching, guiding, and supporting our newest hires, learning how we think about experiment design, dataset generation, time series analysis, feature engineering, and model building for financial datasets.

At Jane Street, our researchers, engineers, and traders sit a few feet away from each other and work together to train models, architect systems, and run trading strategies. We work with petabytes of data, a computing cluster with hundreds of thousands of cores, and a growing GPU cluster containing tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. Depending on the day, we might be diving deep into market data, tuning hyperparameters, debugging distributed training performance, or studying how our model likes to trade in production.

We don’t believe in “one-size-fits-all” modelling solutions; we are open to and excited about applying all different types of statistical and ML techniques, from linear models to deep learning, depending on what best fits a given problem. The most successful researchers will be driven by a curiosity for how their contributions fit into the larger picture of our trading operations, and how to adapt their findings into actionable strategies.

About you

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. If you have a curious mind and a passion for solving interesting problems, we have a feeling you’ll fit right in. You should be:

  • Able to apply logical and mathematical thinking to all kinds of problems
  • Intellectually curious; eager to ask questions, admit mistakes, and learn new things 
  • A strong programmer who’s comfortable with Python
  • An open-minded thinker and precise communicator who enjoys collaborating with colleagues from a wide range of backgrounds and areas of expertise
  • Fluent in English

Most candidates will have experience with data science or machine learning, but ultimately, we’re more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. PhD or other research experience is a plus.

If you’d like to learn more, you can read about our interview process and meet some of the team.

Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

The Team:

As AI tools drive immense value across the firm, our organization faces a "Dual Mandate": providing low-friction access to the best frontier AI tools while strictly managing an exponentially growing cost curve. The unified AI Platform Team builds the centralized software, operations, and governance layers that safely route users to the most cost-effective models.

The Role:

We are looking for a Platform Engineer to help build and operationalize our AI tooling ecosystem. Working closely with the Team Lead and Senior/Staff SWE, you will be the hands-on integrator connecting external cloud AI providers, internal models, and end-user tools into our unified control plane.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Configure and manage multi-engine API gateways, implementing dynamic routing rules, rate limits, and fallback logic for LLM requests.
  • Execute the technical migration and integration of firm-wide tools into our centralized management plane to ensure all AI traffic is securely logged and governed.
  • Operate within our Shared Responsibility Model alongside the Cloud team to manage AI services deployed in enterprise landing zones (e.g., managing Azure OpenAI instances, model deployments, and API key generation).
  • Write robust Go and Python code to support the continuous sync loop for our usage dashboard and implement automated "progressive friction" mechanisms, such as alerts.
  • Partner with the Inference Infrastructure pod to ensure our self-hosted, on-premise models are successfully registered and routable within our AI gateways.

Required Qualifications:

  • Strong backend programming experience, specifically in Go and/or Python.
  • Hands-on experience with API design, integration, and platform/cloud engineering concepts.
  • Familiarity with API gateways, proxy configuration, or distributed system networking.
  • A strong interest in the rapidly evolving LLM ecosystem and the technical mechanics of AI tooling.
  • A collaborative mindset with a focus on writing clean, maintainable code to replace prototype systems.

We are seeking a Senior Analyst, Business Systems Analysis, to lead the delivery of innovative application solutions that support the operations and scalability of our Brookfield Wealth Solutions and Brookfield Credit business areas.   • Partner with business stakeholders to translate requirements into effective, technology-driven solutions.
  • Communicate complex application engineering processes, architectures, and solutions to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure initiatives are executed in alignment with broader technology and business goals/standards.
  • Support end users in using data and applications for performing daily operations.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Management, Business Administration/Commerce, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in product ownership and business systems analysis with specialization in the Asset Management or Insurance industry.
  • Proven experience supporting application and data solutions within investment management and insurance domains, across public and private asset classes.
  • Experience with Investment management & Insurance business domains, specifically in terms of application and data models across Public and Private asset classes
  • Experience with Asset Management applications such as Aladdin/ADC, Clearwater/LPX, WSO, SS&C PLM, Mercatus, Numerix, TriOptima, Bloomberg AIM, and Duco.

Brookfield Wealth Solutions (“BWS”; NYSE/TSX: BNT) is focused on securing the financial futures of individuals and institutions through a range of retirement services, wealth protection products and tailored capital solutions. Through our operating subsidiaries, we offer a broad range of insurance products and services, including annuities, personal and commercial property and casualty insurance and life insurance

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

Reporting to the Director, Derivatives & Markets, we are seeking a Trading Analyst to join Brookfield Wealth Solutions Global Derivative and Markets team. This is a front-office role with broad exposure to FX and rates markets, derivative instruments, trading counterparties, and internal and external stakeholders. The successful candidate will support the team with trade structuring and execution, trade booking and lifecycle management, market analysis, derivatives systems, data and file management, and reporting, while helping ensure the trading function operates efficiently and accurately.

The role is well suited to someone who has developed a foundational understanding of FX and interest rate markets and is looking to deepen their markets and derivatives expertise in a hands-on trading environment.

Responsibilities

Trading & Execution Support

  • Execution of FX and interest rate transactions across relevant products and markets.
  • Assist with pre-trade preparation, including gathering market levels, reviewing pricing, and coordinating execution requirements.
  • Engage with banks and other trading counterparties to obtain pricing, market colour, and relevant execution information.
  • Accurate and timely trade capture and booking across internal trading and derivatives systems.
  • Support ongoing management of the hedge portfolio, including rebalancing, roll strategy, restructuring, as well as collateral and liquidity management
  • Monitor executed transactions and work with relevant teams to resolve trade booking, confirmation, settlement, or other lifecycle issues.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation relating to trading activity.

Modelling and analytics

  • Model derivatives trades and structures to support pricing, hedge design, and investment decisions
  • Build and maintain desk tools for pricing, position data, and analysis
  • Assist with models for stress testing and scenario analysis
  • Assist with pricing new investments and insurance/reinsurance transactions

Markets & Analytics

  • Monitor FX and interest rate markets, including spot and forward markets, yield curves, central bank developments, economic data, and other relevant market drivers.
  • Assist the team with market analysis and preparation of materials to support trading and risk-management decisions.
  • Develop and maintain market data, pricing, exposure, and trading-related analytics.
  • Produce regular and ad hoc reporting on trading activity, market developments, exposures, execution, and other relevant metrics.
  • Build familiarity with the valuation and risk characteristics of FX and rates derivatives and continue developing technical knowledge of relevant products.

Systems, Data & Process Management

  • Support the effective use and maintenance of trading, derivatives, market data, and risk-management systems.
  • Maintain trading files, market data, transaction records, and other front-office information in an accurate and organized manner.
  • Assist with data validation, reconciliations, and investigation of discrepancies across front-office systems and reporting.
  • Identify opportunities to improve, automate, and streamline trading workflows, reporting, and data management.

Stakeholder Management

  • Develop effective working relationships with a broad range of internal stakeholders, including Risk, Operations, Treasury, Finance, Legal, Technology, and other investment and business teams.
  • Develop and maintain professional relationships with external counterparties, including bank salespeople, traders, and other market participants.
  • Coordinate across teams to resolve time-sensitive trading, booking, systems, and operational matters.
  • Communicate clearly and professionally in a fast-paced environment where accuracy, responsiveness, and judgment are important.

Qualifications & Requirements:

  • 2–5 years of relevant experience in financial markets, ideally within a trading, markets, treasury, investment management, banking, or related environment.
  • Foundational understanding of foreign exchange and interest rate markets and the key factors that drive them.
  • Familiarity with relevant derivative instruments, which may include FX spot, forwards, swaps, options, interest rate swaps, cross-currency swaps, and other FX and rates derivatives.
  • Experience with trading, derivatives, risk-management, or market data systems is preferred.
  • Strong understanding of full trade lifecycle events including booking, valuation, settlement, and reporting
  • Strong quantitative and analytical capabilities, with a high level of proficiency in Excel and an ability to work comfortably with financial and market data.
  • Experience with Bloomberg and/or similar market information platforms is preferred.
  • Exposure to Python, VBA, SQL, or other data and automation tools would be an asset but is not required.
  • Strong attention to detail and a demonstrated ability to maintain accuracy while managing multiple priorities.

Join our global team of cyber security experts, protecting our business and developing exciting capabilities on the frontline of cyber defense.  Apply your passion and knowledge of cyber security to assist in the investigation of incidents.  The Cyber Operations Analyst needs to demonstrate thoughtful knowledge of the evolving cyber threat landscape, BlackRock’s risks, controls and security thresholds and recognize the expertise and importance of differentiated roles within the SOC.    More specifically, the Analyst will support the global Cyber Operations function and have following key responsibilities:

  • Intermediate knowledge of Windows and Unix or Linux.

  • Intermediate knowledge of malware operation and indicators. 
  • Intermediate knowledge of penetration techniques.

Here, you’ll find a collaborative culture that respects and values differences and colleagues who share a spirit of generosity.  

Join us for the opportunity to grow and make a difference in ways that matter to you. 

Role Summary 

The Data Product Owner plays a key role within Individual Investors Data Management. The II business is responsible for over $200B in client assets and serves 1.3 million investors. The Data Product Owner leads assigned Retail client data priorities and workstreams, translating business and consumer needs into prioritized capabilities and guiding delivery to ensure client data is accurate, consistent, trusted, and fit for purpose across business processes and downstream consumers/platforms. 

As a Product Owner and subject matter expert in Retail client data, this role serves as a primary partner to business and technology stakeholders, translating complex business needs into clear requirements, priorities, and actionable solutions. The role guides data capabilities through discovery, delivery, and adoption while managing competing priorities and dependencies. Through strong product ownership and data management expertise, the Data Product Owner balances business value, data quality, governance, risk, and scalability when prioritizing work and making decisions. The role drives continuous improvement to strengthen data usability, reliability, and value across the organization. 

Responsibilities 

  • Acts as the Product Owner and primary point of contact for assigned client data domain, partnering across business, technology, analytics, operations, and risk teams to understand needs, resolve issues, and improve data outcomes.  
  • Serves as a consultant to business stakeholders on complex client data needs, translating business objectives into clear product requirements and recommending solutions that support informed decision-making and operational effectiveness.  
  • Owns and prioritizes the backlog for assigned scope, balancing business value, data quality, risk, dependencies, and delivery capacity to make informed trade-off recommendations.  
  • Partners with engineering, architecture, analytics, and business teams throughout product discovery, refinement, delivery, validation, and adoption.  
  • Ensures product requirements incorporate applicable data governance, quality, control, metadata, and enterprise standards throughout the product lifecycle.  
  • Defines acceptance criteria and leads business validation and UAT for new or enhanced product capabilities, ensuring delivered solutions meet business and data requirements.  
  • Defines and monitors product success measures, including adoption, data quality, reliability, and business value, and uses results to inform continuous improvement priorities.  
  • Proactively identifies and manages data quality issues, risks, and dependencies within assigned products, driving remediation in alignment with enterprise policies, standards, and procedures.  
  • Provides guidance, knowledge sharing, and support to less experienced associates and serves as a resource for data management and product ownership best practices.

Role Summary

The AI Product Manager will lead some of Global Distribution’s most consequential AI-enabled transformations, beginning with fundamental questions about how client experiences, commercial activities, and business workflows should operate in an AI-native world and carrying those ideas through to measurable business outcomes.

Reporting directly to the Head of Global Distribution AI Strategy & Transformation, this role will own one or more high-conviction transformation opportunities that require dedicated incubation and sustained cross-functional leadership. These initiatives may span business processes, client experiences, data, technology, roles, controls, and ways of working and will often develop over multiple quarters.

The AI Product Manager is expected to begin with the future state rather than the existing process: if this experience or workflow were being designed from scratch today, knowing what artificial intelligence can now make possible, how should it work?

From there, the role is accountable for turning that ambition into reality—building conviction around the vision, defining the business case and product strategy, sequencing a practical roadmap, making difficult product and design decisions, partnering with Technology and Data through delivery, driving organizational change, and demonstrating realized business value.

This is not a traditional backlog-management role. The AI Product Manager is a senior transformation leader who combines strategic imagination, product judgment, business acumen, AI fluency, and execution discipline to create materially different ways of working.

Responsibilities

Reimagine the Future:

  • Start with the business or client problem and develop a bold, coherent point of view on how the experience or workflow should operate as AI capabilities continue to advance.
  • Challenge assumptions embedded in existing processes, technology limitations, roles, handoffs, and operating models rather than simply automating the current state.
  • Develop a deep understanding of client needs, Associate workflows, business economics, data, technology, risk, and competitive dynamics relevant to the opportunity.
  • Translate emerging AI capabilities into practical strategic possibilities, identifying where AI can fundamentally change the experience rather than merely make existing activities faster.
  • Create clarity around what should remain distinctly human, what should be AI-enabled, what can be automated, and what work may no longer need to exist.

Turn the Vision into a Product Strategy:

  • Define the product vision, target-state experience or workflow, value proposition, business case, success measures, and strategic roadmap required to bring the transformation to life.
  • Break a large future-state ambition into a sequence of valuable releases and decisions that create momentum while preserving the long-term vision.
  • Establish clear product priorities and make deliberate trade-offs across business value, client experience, speed, scope, data, technology, risk, cost, and organizational readiness.
  • Translate ambiguous business needs into sufficiently clear product requirements, design principles, workflows, and decisions for Technology, Data, Design, Risk, and other delivery partners.
  • Continuously evolve the roadmap as AI capabilities, user needs, technical feasibility, and organizational learning change.

Lead End-to-End Delivery:

  • Maintain end-to-end accountability for the transformation from early concept through design, engineering delivery, launch, adoption, and ongoing evolution.
  • Serve as the primary connection across business leaders, Technology, Data, Design, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and other enterprise partners required to deliver the product.
  • Engage credibly in architecture, data, build-vs.-buy, integration, model, and design discussions and ensure technical decisions preserve the intended business outcome and sufficient flexibility for future evolution.
  • Drive timely resolution of blockers, dependencies, competing priorities, and difficult trade-offs across a complex matrixed organization.
  • Preserve clarity of objectives and accountability through delivery handoffs; ensure that technical completion is not mistaken for successful delivery when the intended business outcome has not been achieved.
  • Maintain urgency and momentum without sacrificing the quality, controls, or enterprise readiness required for durable solutions.

Make the Transformation Real:

  • Build strong business sponsorship and engage the Associates, managers, and leaders whose work or client experience will change as a result of the product.
  • Partner with change, learning, and business teams to redesign roles, processes, procedures, incentives, controls, and ways of working required to capture the full value of the product.
  • Own the business case and expected value outcomes for the transformation, including appropriate measures of client impact, commercial outcomes, productivity, capacity, quality, cost, adoption, or other relevant results.
  • Partner with the AI Portfolio, Governance & Value Realization team to establish consistent measurement while retaining direct accountability for whether the product delivers its expected value.
  • Use evidence from adoption and realized outcomes to improve the product, change course when required, and make recommendations to scale, accelerate, rethink, or stop investments.
  • Capture broader lessons and reusable capabilities that can inform other AI products, targeted workflow transformations, and the broader GD AI ecosystem.

Mindset

  • Starts with the blank sheet of paper. Naturally asks how the business should work in the future rather than accepting the current state as the starting constraint.
  • Strategic and imaginative. Can connect emerging AI capabilities with client needs, business strategy, workflows, and operating-model possibilities others may not immediately see.
  • Makes ideas real. Enjoys the hard work of translating an ambitious vision into decisions, roadmaps, products, organizational change, and measurable outcomes.
  • Intellectually curious. Quickly develops depth across unfamiliar business, technology, data, and AI topics and asks incisive questions of experts.
  • High ownership. Does not stop at a recommendation, specification, engineering handoff, or launch; remains accountable for the business outcome.
  • Comfortable in ambiguity. Creates clarity and forward motion without waiting for perfect information.
  • AI-forward. Actively experiments with and learns from rapidly evolving AI capabilities so that the vision of what is possible continues to expand.
  • Influential without relying on authority. Builds conviction, challenges constructively, and aligns senior stakeholders across a complex matrix.
  • Low ego and team-oriented. Seeks the best answer rather than personal ownership of the answer and builds strong partnerships with business and technical teams.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, technology, engineering, economics, design, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred and 8+ years of related experience
  • Experience across product management, strategy, business transformation, management consulting, digital transformation, innovation, or related roles.
  • Demonstrated experience taking ambiguous, strategically important problems from initial concept through implementation and measurable business outcomes.
  • Proven ability to develop compelling product visions and translate them into actionable roadmaps, priorities, requirements, and delivery decisions.
  • Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives spanning business, technology, data, and organizational change.
  • Strong business judgment and ability to develop business cases, identify value drivers, and make difficult investment and prioritization trade-offs.
  • Strong understanding of generative AI, large language models, agentic workflows, and emerging AI-enabled business models and experiences.
  • Sufficient technical fluency to engage credibly with engineers, architects, data leaders, and AI specialists on architecture and implementation trade-offs.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills and demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders.

Preferred:

  • Experience in asset management, financial services, distribution, sales, marketing, client service, or another complex client-facing environment.
  • Experience building AI-enabled products or transforming workflows using generative AI in a complex enterprise setting.
  • Experience owning the full product lifecycle from vision and incubation through production, adoption, and ongoing optimization.
  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture, data governance, privacy, responsible AI, risk management, and regulated product-development environments.
  • Track record of delivering measurable improvements in client experience, revenue or commercial outcomes, productivity, capacity, quality, or cost.

The AI Ecosystem & Distributed Innovation Lead will build and scale the environment that enables Global Distribution Associates to create reusable value with AI.

Reporting to the Director, AI Enablement & Ecosystem, this role will own the strategy and operating model for Associate-built reusable AI solutions, including Skills, assistants, agents, templates, playbooks, and emerging capabilities made possible by enterprise AI platforms.

The role will apply a product-management mindset to the broader GD AI ecosystem: understanding what Associates are building and using, identifying the highest-value solutions, helping creators improve promising capabilities, developing approaches to validation and responsible sharing, expanding the enterprise toolkit, and making successful solutions easy for others to discover and adopt.

The role will also serve as a visible AI evangelist across GD, translating fast-moving technology developments into practical opportunities and creating excitement and momentum around what Associates can now accomplish.

Responsibilities

Distributed Innovation Strategy:

  • Own the vision and roadmap for Associate-built reusable AI solutions across Global Distribution.
  • Develop mechanisms that encourage broad experimentation and creation while focusing attention on recurring business needs and high-value use cases.
  • Understand how Associates are using available AI capabilities, identify common patterns, and determine where central-team support can significantly improve quality or scale.
  • Establish measures of ecosystem health, including creation, reuse, adoption, engagement, quality, and demonstrated business value.

Reusable Solution Lifecycle:

  • Build a scalable lifecycle to discover, assess, improve, validate, publish, promote, measure, maintain, and retire reusable AI solutions.
  • Identify high-potential Associate-created solutions and partner with their creators to improve reliability, usability, instructions, evaluations, documentation, and scalability.
  • Develop clear standards for when a solution can be broadly shared or endorsed within GD.
  • Define criteria and pathways for graduating successful solutions into targeted workflow interventions or formal AI products when usage, complexity, risk, data requirements, or business importance warrant greater investment.

AI Ecosystem & Capability Roadmap:

  • Maintain a deep understanding of enterprise-approved AI platforms, tools, connectors, agent capabilities, and emerging functionality.
  • Identify gaps between available capabilities and the needs of GD Associates and reusable-solution creators.
  • Translate those gaps into clear business requirements and roadmap priorities for Technology, Data, enterprise AI teams, Labs, and platform providers.
  • Evaluate new capabilities through practical experimentation and determine where they can unlock meaningful new use cases or improve existing solutions.

Responsible Scaling & Risk Management:

  • Partner with Technology, Data, Risk, Legal, Compliance, and other control functions to establish practical guardrails for Associate-built reusable AI solutions.
  • Help creators understand appropriate use of enterprise data, approved tools, validation expectations, and other relevant controls.
  • Balance broad innovation and speed with appropriate management of operational, data, privacy, compliance, and AI-related risks.
  • Identify systemic barriers to distributed innovation and work with enterprise partners to resolve them.

Activation, Adoption & Community Engagement:

  • Make emerging AI capabilities understandable and exciting to Associates through examples, demos, showcases, experimentation, and practical storytelling.
  • Partner with the AI Learning & Community Enablement Lead and AI Champions to identify creators, spread best practices, and drive adoption of high-value reusable solutions.
  • Develop an effective internal discovery experience or catalog so Associates can find solutions relevant to their work.
  • Build a strong community of AI-forward builders and power users who help expand innovation beyond the capacity of the central team.

Mindset

  • Highly AI-forward, curious, and hands-on; learns new capabilities by experimenting with them.
  • Product thinker who obsesses over users, quality, adoption, and continuous improvement.

  • Comfortable balancing rapid innovation with enterprise risk and control requirements.

Role Summary

The AI Adoption & Integration Lead will help Associates and managers successfully transition to AI-enabled ways of working and embed those changes into their day-to-day routines, roles, behaviors, and operating practices.

As a core member of a dedicated Implementation Pod, this role will work alongside the business team, AI Process Transformation Lead, and Applied AI Solutions Lead throughout each engagement. The AI Adoption & Integration Lead will bring the perspective of the people whose work is changing, helping the team understand what it will take for the new workflow to be practical, trusted, adopted, and sustained.

This role is not primarily about communications or delivering training after a solution has already been designed. The AI Adoption & Integration Lead will participate throughout the engagement so that user needs, change implications, and adoption risks can influence the emerging workflow and solution in real time.

Success will be measured by whether real people successfully adopt the new way of working and whether the business can sustain it after the Implementation Pod moves on.

Responsibilities

Understand the People:

  • Build trusted relationships with the Associates, managers, and business leaders whose work is changing and understand how the proposed change will affect their day-to-day experience.
  • Identify likely adoption barriers, skill gaps, concerns, incentives, role impacts, and practical realities that need to influence the future-state design.
  • Bring the user and people perspective into Pod discussions throughout the engagement rather than waiting until launch.
  • Help the team distinguish between reasonable adoption concerns and change resistance that requires active leadership reinforcement.

Prepare People for the Change:

  • Develop a focused adoption approach tailored to the specific workflow, population, and business context, including communications, hands-on learning, manager enablement, job aids, and launch support.
  • Translate the emerging workflow and AI solution into practical guidance that Associates can understand and use confidently.
  • Help users understand when and how to use AI effectively, where human judgment remains important, and how to respond when the solution does not behave as expected.
  • Partner closely with business managers and workflow stewards so they are equipped to reinforce the new way of working.

Make the New Way of Working Stick:

  • Ensure responsibilities, procedures, escalation paths, operating routines, and ongoing ownership are clear before the Pod completes an engagement.
  • Support launch, gather rapid feedback from users, and work with Pod teammates to address adoption barriers or practical issues as they emerge.
  • Establish practical adoption and usage measures and support post-launch assessment of whether the new workflow is being sustained.
  • Capture reusable change and adoption practices and share recurring learning with the broader AI Learning & Community Enablement team.

Mindset

  • People-oriented and empathetic: naturally seeks to understand how change will affect others and what they need to be successful.
  • Builds trust quickly and is comfortable engaging with people doing real jobs, not only senior stakeholders.
  • Brings positive energy, optimism, and momentum to change.
  • Strong listener and facilitator who can help people move from uncertainty to confidence.
  • Organized and execution-oriented; follows through on the many practical details that determine whether change sticks.
  • AI-forward and enthusiastic about helping others become successful with new technology.
  • High urgency, low ego, and excited to be part of a high-performing team rather than seeking individual ownership or visibility.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in business, organizational development, communications, human resources, operations, technology, or a related discipline and 5+ years of related experience.
  • Experience in change management, digital adoption, transformation, implementation, learning, organizational effectiveness, or related roles.
  • Demonstrated experience helping teams adopt new technology, processes, or ways of working.
  • Strong interpersonal, facilitation, communication, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Ability to translate complex changes into simple, practical guidance for business users.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to execute quickly in a fast-moving team environment.
  • Working knowledge of generative AI and enthusiasm for helping others use AI effectively.

Preferred:

  • Experience supporting technology-enabled workflow transformation.
  • Experience developing and facilitating hands-on learning or adoption programs.
  • Experience in financial services, asset management, or another regulated environment.
  • Familiarity with change-management methodologies, applied pragmatically rather than as rigid process.

FINRA Requirements

FINRA licenses are not required and will not be supported for this role.

Work Flexibility

This role is eligible for hybrid work, with up to one day per week from home.

Role Summary

The AI Process Transformation Lead will help Global Distribution teams fundamentally improve how work gets done by combining deep process understanding with the opportunities created by artificial intelligence.

As a senior member of a dedicated Implementation Pod, this role will work directly alongside the business team, Applied AI Solutions Lead, and AI Adoption & Integration Lead during focused engagements. The AI Process Transformation Lead will rapidly develop a fact-based understanding of the current workflow, identify the highest-value points of leverage, and co-design a materially better future state.

The role requires someone who can quickly make sense of complex and unfamiliar work: understanding activities, volumes, decisions, handoffs, exceptions, controls, systems, and performance, while challenging assumptions about what can be a candidate for change.

This is not a traditional requirements-gathering or business-analysis position. The AI Process Transformation Lead is a senior transformation practitioner who helps the business reimagine its work and stays deeply engaged through implementation.

Responsibilities

Understand the Work:

  • Rapidly get to the core of how a business workflow operates today through direct engagement with the Associates and leaders who perform and manage the work.
  • Map the critical activities, inputs, outputs, volumes, decisions, handoffs, systems, controls, exceptions, bottlenecks, and recurring sources of effort or friction.
  • Establish practical performance baselines and identify the portions of the workflow where improvement could create meaningful business value.
  • Distinguish root causes from symptoms and challenge assumptions about why existing activities, approvals, or handoffs exist.

Reimagine the Work:

  • Co-design the target-state workflow alongside the business team and Applied AI Solutions Lead, combining deep knowledge of how the work operates today with emerging AI capabilities to create a materially better future state.
  • Determine which elements of the workflow should be simplified, eliminated, automated, AI-augmented, or fundamentally reimagined.
  • Translate the future-state design into clear roles, decisions, handoffs, exception paths, controls, and measures of success.
  • Maintain a strong focus on the primary business outcome and resist unnecessary complexity or scope expansion.

Deliver and Learn at Pace:

  • Stay actively involved through rapid build, testing, iteration, launch, and handoff rather than treating process design as a front-end deliverable.
  • Work with real users to test the proposed future state and adapt the workflow as the team learns what works in practice.
  • Partner with the AI Adoption & Integration Lead to ensure the redesigned process can be understood, adopted, and sustained by the business.
  • Capture reusable process patterns and lessons that can accelerate future engagements or identify opportunities for broader transformation.

Mindset

  • Analytical and structured: naturally seeks facts, patterns, clarity, and measurable evidence.
  • Organized and grounded: quickly turns messy work into an understandable operating model.
  • Insatiably curious about how work actually happens.
  • Comfortable getting into operational detail without losing sight of the business outcome.
  • Challenges legacy assumptions respectfully and constructively.
  • AI-forward, while remaining focused on solving the problem rather than forcing AI into it.
  • High urgency, low ego, and energized by solving a succession of different business problems as part of a team.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in business, operations, engineering, finance, information systems, or a related discipline and 8+ years of related experience.
  • Experience in process transformation, operations, management consulting, continuous improvement, business architecture, or related roles.
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading the analysis and redesign of complex business workflows.
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including experience establishing performance baselines and measurable target outcomes.
  • Ability to rapidly learn unfamiliar business domains and ask incisive questions of subject-matter experts.
  • Strong facilitation and stakeholder-management skills across frontline, management, and senior-leadership audiences.
  • Working understanding of generative AI, automation, and emerging AI-enabled workflows.

Preferred:

  • Experience in asset management, financial services, or another regulated environment.
  • Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, process engineering, service design, or related disciplines.
  • Experience implementing technology-enabled transformation rather than only developing recommendations.
  • Familiarity with process-mapping, process-mining, workflow, or analytical tools.

The Director, Applied AI will lead Global Distribution's dedicated capability for rapidly applying artificial intelligence to targeted business workflows.

Reporting to the Head of Global Distribution AI Strategy & Transformation, this leader will manage two permanent, multidisciplinary Implementation Pods. Each Pod will bring together an AI Process Transformation Lead, an Applied AI Solutions Lead, and an AI Adoption & Integration Lead to work side-by-side with a committed business team.

The Director is accountable for making this model work repeatedly and at pace: selecting the right engagements, creating the conditions for successful co-creation with the business, maintaining a high bar for execution, removing blockers, and building a team that becomes faster and more effective with every sprint.

This is not a traditional program-management role. The Director will lead a hands-on transformation capability that moves quickly from understanding a workflow to designing, building, launching, and embedding a materially better way of working.

Responsibilities

Build a High-Performing Applied AI Capability:

  • Lead two permanent Implementation Pods that rapidly redesign targeted workflows using approved AI tools and enterprise capabilities.
  • Establish a simple, repeatable delivery approach that preserves urgency, deep business partnership, clear accountability, and measurable outcomes.
  • Build a team culture defined by high standards, low ego, intellectual curiosity, rapid learning, and shared accountability for the result.
  • Ensure the Process Transformation, AI Solutions, Adoption, and business perspectives are tightly integrated throughout each engagement.

Select the Right Pod Engagements:

  • Partner across the GD AI team to select opportunities that are focused enough to move quickly, meaningful enough to matter, measurable within a reasonable period, and feasible using approved tools, data, and control boundaries.
  • Ensure genuine business pull before beginning an engagement: a committed business owner and workflow steward, dedicated Associate capacity carved out to support the sprint, active participation throughout design and testing, and a ready/willing/able commitment to adopt and sustain the resulting way of working.
  • Redirect opportunities that are too broad, immature, technically complex, or insufficiently sponsored to the appropriate alternative delivery path rather than forcing them through the Pod model.

Drive Fast, High-Quality Execution:

  • Maintain accountability for the overall quality, pace, and outcomes of Pod engagements from kickoff through launch and handoff.
  • Help teams make rapid, pragmatic decisions when information is incomplete, while ensuring material data, technology, risk, or control issues are addressed appropriately.
  • Remove blockers and secure timely support from Technology, Data, Risk, business leaders, and other partners when needed.
  • Keep teams focused on the primary business outcome rather than allowing engagements to expand into unnecessary scope or complexity.

Make the Model Better Every Time:

  • Capture reusable process, AI, adoption, and delivery patterns that allow future engagements to move faster and produce stronger outcomes.
  • Coach and develop Pod members so they build increasing judgment, versatility, and confidence across a wide variety of business challenges.
  • Identify recurring opportunities that should become reusable AI capabilities or larger transformational products rather than repeatedly solved one workflow at a time.
  • Partner with the AI Portfolio, Governance & Value Realization team to assess adoption and realized business impact after launch.

Mindset

  • Creates urgency without creating chaos.
  • Highly AI-forward and excited by what rapidly evolving capabilities make possible.
  • Values team outcomes over individual heroics or functional ownership.
  • Comfortable moving from one unfamiliar business problem to another and helping the team get smart quickly.
  • Pragmatic: seeks the simplest approach capable of delivering meaningful value.
  • Believes the business must co-create the solution and ultimately own the resulting way of working.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in business transformation, AI/digital implementation, operations, product delivery, management consulting, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated track record leading multidisciplinary teams through fast-paced, measurable transformation.
  • Experience redesigning workflows spanning people, process, data, and technology.

Role Summary

The Director, AI Enablement & Ecosystem will lead the capabilities that enable Global Distribution (GD) to adopt, scale, and continuously expand the value created through artificial intelligence.

Reporting to the Head of Global Distribution AI Strategy & Transformation, this leader will oversee the operating system that supports the GD AI portfolio, including intake and prioritization, governance and value realization, scaled learning and adoption, the AI Champions and broader community ecosystem, and the development of Associate-built reusable AI solutions.

The role will lead a small team with distinct accountability for portfolio and governance, AI ecosystem and distributed innovation, and learning and community enablement. The Director will connect these capabilities into an integrated system that makes it easy for Associates to identify opportunities, build AI fluency, create and adopt reusable solutions, and demonstrate measurable business value.

The position will partner closely with AI Product Managers, the Applied AI & Implementation team, business leaders, Technology, Data, Risk, Human Resources, enterprise AI teams, and external platform partners.

Responsibilities

AI Enablement Strategy & Operating Model:

  • Translate the GD AI strategy into an integrated roadmap for scaled enablement, distributed innovation, portfolio management, and adoption.
  • Establish the operating model, standards, processes, and decision rights required to support AI activity across Global Distribution.
  • Ensure the function evolves as AI capabilities, enterprise platforms, Associate needs, and regulatory and risk requirements change.
  • Create clear connections across the GD AI portfolio so that lessons from Associate experimentation, targeted workflow interventions, and transformational products inform one another.

Portfolio, Governance & Value Realization:

  • Oversee an always-on intake and prioritization capability that enables Associates and leaders to easily surface high-value AI opportunities.
  • Maintain transparent portfolio governance and decision processes that concentrate scarce resources on opportunities with the strongest combination of value, readiness, feasibility, and strategic importance.
  • Establish consistent expectations for business cases, success measures, baselines, adoption metrics, and realized-value tracking across AI initiatives.
  • Support senior governance forums with clear portfolio reporting, decisions, risks, dependencies, and evidence of measurable business impact.

AI Ecosystem & Distributed Innovation:

  • Own the strategy for enabling Associates to create, discover, improve, share, and adopt reusable AI solutions using approved enterprise capabilities.

The Opportunity 

If you enjoy applying your quantitative and ML skills to real-world problems, coding production-quality analysis and tools, and working in a fast-paced environment with immediate and tangible feedback, our Summer Internship Program is ideal for you. 

At Brevan Howard, we build systematic and discretionary investment processes that rely on rigorous analysis of a vast universe of data, such as asset prices, macroeconomic indicators, news, sell-side research, and trading signals. Transforming this data into actionable insights is central to how we win, and we’re looking to find the next generation of portfolio managers and quants through our internship program—people who are eager to push the frontier of research and engineering in global macro investing. 

Overview & Responsibilities 

You will work directly with our front-office personnel to provide immediate impact on a range of projects: 

  • Build pipelines to extract and analyze data, develop models and trading signals, and support decision-making of Portfolio Managers.

  • Integrate AI into analytical systems as well as building new AI-powered tools using the latest LLMs and agent workflows. 

  • Contribute to our core analytics library, which is leveraged by Quants and PMs across the firm for research, trading and risk management. 

  • Our Internship Program starts with one-week in-depth training to prepare interns for the desk. This covers a range of topics relating to Financial Markets including Macroeconomics, FX, Digital Assets, Interest Rate Derivatives, Equity Rates, Bonds, Credit and Fixed Income, Trading Strategies, Risk Management, Excel and Python, and the latest AI tools and LLMs. 

  • During the program, working in a fast-paced environment, Interns will contribute to their Portfolio Management teams on various projects that can include trading strategies, trading signals, back testing, developing market related models, and develop research for trade ideas. 

  • Additionally, interns will benefit from key talks, a mentor program, social events and interactions with some of the most respected and talented individuals in their field. 

  • This internship is devised to provide candidates with an invaluable education on the workings of a macro hedge fund and the regulatory environment through a two-way process to determine if Brevan Howard and the intern are a compatible fit. 

  • The goal of our summer internship program is to convert top performing interns to our 2028 Graduate Program! 

Qualifications & Requirements 

​

  • A Ph.D. candidate or 1st year master’s student at a recognized University — completed and awarded before July 2028. 

  • Strong mathematical, quantitative, problem-solving capabilities, and technical skills in Excel, VBA, and R. 

  • Programming experience in Python. 

  • An interest and passion for financial markets, trading, and financial products. 

  • The ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team 

  • An entrepreneurial spirit. 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. 

Why take this opportunity 

This is a unique opportunity to gain insight into one of the world’s leading firms operating at the forefront of macro trading. At Brevan Howard, we believe the future of investing lies at the intersection of deep domain expertise and cutting-edge technology. As our industry is being reshaped by AI and automation, you’ll see first-hand how LLMs, retrieval, and agent-like systems are being used in the front-office environment at one of the world’s premier macro hedge funds – where correctness, robustness and speed matter. 

Top-performing interns are considered for our Graduate Program the following year and longer-term paths include roles as analyst, quant, and portfolio manager. 

Please note that you may only submit one application to the Summer Internship Program globally. We encourage you to apply to the role and region that best align with your skills, experience, and interests.    

 

Compensation 

Compensation for this internship is based on an annualized salary of $200,000, prorated for the 10-week duration of the program. All interns also receive a housing stipend and an internship completion bonus.

  • Automation & Standards: Build and maintain automation, standards, reference architectures, and documentation that strengthen deployment consistency and enable teams to consume cloud services safely and consistently.
  • Integration & Collaboration: Engineer and support resilient cloud connectivity, including transit architectures and connectivity between cloud providers and on-premises environments.
  • Observability & Monitoring: Implement and improve observability across cloud services, including metrics, logs, traces, alerting, and capacity dashboards.
  • Stakeholder Support: Advise application and infrastructure teams on cloud, hybrid, and on-premises architecture choices based on reliability, performance, security, and cost.
  • Cost Management: Partner with Finance and Purchasing on cloud cost visibility, forecasting, and commitments, holding yourself accountable for the team's FinOps and efficiency goals.
  • Continuous Improvement: Research, evaluate, and implement new cloud services and capabilities that improve reliability, developer experience, security, or efficiency.

What We're Looking For:

  • Strong knowledge of cloud networking, including VPCs, routing, DNS, firewalls, load balancing, private connectivity, and interconnect providers.
  • Working knowledge of cloud security fundamentals, including IAM, encryption/key management, secrets management, and least-privilege design.
  • Experience with cloud observability, monitoring, and alerting, and a proven ability to troubleshoot and resolve complex production problems while making sound decisions under pressure.
  • Understanding of cloud cost models and practical approaches to cost allocation, optimization, capacity planning, and FinOps.
  • Excellent communication and documentation skills, with the ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and adapt to changing technologies and business needs while working effectively across technical teams and cloud providers.
  • A proven track record of delivering secure, scalable, and reliable cloud solutions, with strong ownership and accountability for production outcomes.
  • Willingness to participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation supporting production cloud environments.
  • Previous experience in financial services or trading environments is a plus.

About the Role

Wellington's Stewardship & Sustainable Investment team plays a key role in bringing together our sustainable investment capabilities and the firm's stewardship activities, helping to enhance long-term value for our clients. We are seeking a Stewardship Associate to join this collaborative team, which sits within the COO Group on our Investment Platform, as we seek to scale our capabilities across engagement, proxy voting and stewardship operations.  

 

This role will support Wellington's stewardship activities by partnering with investment professionals to execute company engagements, inform proxy voting decisions, and advance research on governance and other financially material sustainability issues. The successful candidate will be highly collaborative and establish credibility across multiple teams to contribute to engagement prioritization, proxy analysis, stewardship reporting, and the scaling of stewardship processes to deliver strong long-term outcomes for clients. 

Responsibilities 

  

Company Engagement 

  • Support the Stewardship Lead in the development and execution of thematic and issuer-specific engagement priorities.  

  • Participate in and lead, where appropriate, engagements with company management and board directors in support of stewardship priorities and to inform proxy voting decisions.   

  • Identify and communicate key insights, company responsiveness, and engagement outcomes.  

  • Contribute to issuer-specific research, stewardship case studies and internal knowledge sharing that support the broader investment dialogue. 

  

Proxy Voting

  • Incorporate company engagement history, investment research, governance practices, and market context into voting analysis, feeding back into development of voting guidelines 

  • Support proxy voting operations, especially during peak proxy season, while helping improve the efficiency and quality of voting workflows. 

  • Monitor regulatory developments and evolving governance practices across global markets. 

  

Stewardship Operations  

  • Maintain accurate engagement records and stewardship data to support reporting, measurement, and transparency. 

  • Leverage data analytics and AI-enabled research tools, where appropriate, to improve the efficiency and quality of proxy voting analysis, engagement capture, and reporting.  

  • Assist with embedding stewardship and sustainable investment capabilities in investor workflows 

  • Support stewardship reporting and responses to stewardship-related RFI/RFPs through close collaboration with teams on the infrastructure and client platforms.

The HRBP will act as a strategic partner to leadership, with a heavy emphasis on organizational design, workforce planning, and scaling teams responsibly. This is a builder's role: you will help define how a large technical organization is structured, leveled, and grown, while providing hands-on support for performance management, employee relations, and leadership development. The ideal candidate will have deep HR experience supporting technical populations at scale, strong business acumen, and the ability to operate in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment.

What you'll do
Work with the Technology and Platform business heads to set the people strategy for those organizations, translating engineering roadmaps and departmental goals into action across hiring, engagement, development, performance, and retention. Lead organizational design for a large, complex technical organization: assess team structures, spans of control, reporting lines, and role definitions, and recommend changes that support scale without adding unnecessary layers. Own workforce planning at scale, building multi-quarter headcount plans by team and skill set, modeling growth scenarios, and pressure-testing plans against budget and delivery commitments. Build and maintain leveling and career frameworks for technical roles, ensuring consistent expectations for individual contributors and managers across engineering, infrastructure, and platform teams. Partner closely with Talent Acquisition on high-volume and specialized technical hiring, setting priorities around headcount sequencing, hiring timelines, role requirements, and candidate experience. Scale onboarding and ramp-up for technical hires, ensuring a smooth transition from offer through full integration, including compliance, systems access, technical environment readiness, and cultural immersion. Hold managers accountable for early talent success, ensuring 30-, 60-, and 90-day milestones are met, development plans are established quickly, and new hires are supported through ramp-up. Grow the people manager bench by identifying emerging leaders, coaching first-time managers, and partnering with the Talent Development Specialist on manager development, technical leadership, and communication skills. Define learning priorities for Technology and Platform with the Talent Development Specialist, co-designing role-based development paths and technical onboarding tracks that map to the leveling framework, and reinforcing application of training with managers. Set and reinforce performance expectations across a large population, guiding managers through goal setting, calibration, performance reviews, feedback cycles, and development planning. Advise leadership on compensation and rewards for technical talent, including market benchmarking, equity and bonus structures, and retention actions for critical contributors. Serve as a trusted people leader for the departments, proactively addressing concerns, navigating sensitive issues, managing escalations, and protecting a high-integrity, high-performance culture. Lead people-side change management for reorganizations, team splits and merges, new platform initiatives, and shifts in operating model, including communication planning and manager enablement. Leverage people data and insights at scale to spot trends, surface risks, and inform leadership decisions related to attrition, performance, engagement, span-of-control, and workforce planning.

What you'll need
Bachelor’s degree in human resources, Business Administration, Organizational Psychology, or related field (Master’s or HR certification a plus). 5+ years of strategic HR Partner role experience. Proven background in big tech, fintech, or high-growth environments is strongly preferred. Strong business acumen: ability to understand trading/investment business dynamics, financial incentives, performance pressure, and cultural sensitivities. Excellent interpersonal communication and influencing skills; ability to build trust and credibility with senior leadership and team members. Strong conflict resolution, coaching, and employee-relations skills. Solid knowledge of employment law, compliance, compensation practices, and HR best practices. Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, manage sensitive/confidential matters, and adapt to changing priorities. Analytical mindset, with ability to use HR data and metrics to drive decision-making and provide insight to leadership. Integrity, discretion, professionalism, and deep respect for confidentiality.

We are looking for the next generation of quantitative investors. We offer a range of opportunities, spanning quantitative research, portfolio management, product strategy and investment technology.

BlackRock Systematic is one of the largest quantitative investment managers in the world, with over $200bn in assets under management and 35+ years of systematic investing experience. We manage hedge funds, long-only active products and outcome-focused portfolios across a wide range of asset classes, geographies and time horizons.

We are constantly evolving to sustain our leadership position in quantitative investing – searching to unlock new opportunities presented by emerging technologies in machine learning and artificial intelligence paired with big(ger) data. We are a pioneer in sustainable investing, a leader in cutting-edge quantitative techniques, and passionate about delivering creative investment solutions for our diverse client base.

Teams you may be considered for:


Factors, Sustainability and Solutions (FS2)
FS2 combines the research and investment expertise across the BlackRock Systematic Investment platform to drive product innovation, product research and client engagement. Products and client solutions range from systematic return-seeking to factor-based, sustainability and outcome-oriented, spanning all asset classes. We constantly identify new product opportunities and develop unique investment models to best serve our clients.

Systematic Active Equity
A pioneering quantitative investment team comprised of industry leaders that applies powerful machine learning techniques to active equity investment strategies. We apply data such as today’s trading activity, internet searches, next year’s economic forecasts and long-term demographic trends to construct optimal high-breadth portfolios across global public equity markets. We partner with top academics to ensure our research techniques are at the forefront of machine learning and artificial intelligence. Systematic Fixed Income

  • Client focus – our clients are our partners, and we are deeply invested in their well-being and success.

  • Sustainability – our approach to sustainability is rooted in our fiduciary duty to our clients, providing choice backed by research, data and analytics to produce the best risk-adjusted returns within client mandates

  • Strong technical problem-solving skills

  • Ability to write efficient, effective computer code (Python)

  • Experience with translating statistical models and algorithms into code

  • Comfort in working with large datasets

  • Inquisitive nature, desire to learn and critical thinking

  • Effective communication and collaboration skills

  • Curiosity, critical thinking, learning agility, and sound judgement in technology-enabled decision making, coupled with an enthusiasm for AI, emerging technologies, and continuous innovation


Your learning and development will include:

  • Contributing to the function’s knowledge base by working on investment or client-related projects

  • Joining daily market-related updates, learning about how our portfolios trade and react to market events

  • Collaborating across multiple business functions to learn the research and product life cycles and our strategies for continued growth

  • Developing an understanding of capital markets, return drivers and economic theory

  • Learning about our clients and their investment strategies; assisting in guiding investors toward achieving their unique investment goals by applying our technology and tools

  • Being part of an innovative, dynamic, diverse team culture and learning from some of the best minds in the business

In this highly visible role, you will work closely with Enterprise Relationship Managers (ERMs), senior technology leaders, and key external executives to oversee a portfolio of strategic vendors that are critical to BlackRock's technology agenda. In your role you will orchestrate an end-to-end strategic technology partner program to maximize business value, increase resilience, and ensure sustained performance from these partnerships. This includes driving vendor performance management, executive engagement, commercial strategy alignment, and governance for each relationship.


Key Responsibilities:


  • Technology Relationship Leadership: Serve as the primary relationship manager for a set of BlackRock’s most strategic technology vendors. You will act as a horizontal leader across the enterprise for these relationships, coordinating all interactions through a “single front door” to the vendor. Develop a deep understanding of each vendor’s product offerings, roadmaps, and strategic fit, and drive alignment between the vendor’s capabilities and BlackRock’s technology strategy.
  • End-to-End Program Oversight: Oversee the full lifecycle of vendor management for your portfolio – from onboarding and risk assessment, through ongoing performance tracking, to contract renewals and strategic reviews. This includes implementing a formal governance framework with regular touchpoints such as Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and executive steering meetings (EBCs) to review performance, risks, and opportunities. Ensure that each vendor has up-to-date relationship artifacts (executive briefs, relationship maps, action logs, KPI scorecards) and that issues or escalations are promptly addressed and resolved.
  • Performance & Risk Management: Drive high service performance and resilience from each vendor. Monitor service delivery against agreed SLAs and KPIs and hold vendors accountable for meeting BlackRock’s expectations for quality, reliability, and security. Proactively identify and mitigate operational risks – ensuring vendors have robust continuity plans and that there are no single points of failure threatening our business. If performance gaps or incidents occur, lead the escalation and corrective action process in partnership with technical teams and risk management (e.g. Technology Risk, Legal & Compliance) to protect BlackRock’s interests.
  • Executive Engagement & Governance: Orchestrate senior-level engagement with each strategic vendor. Collaborate with designated Executive Sponsors ensure they are connected with vendor leadership at the right intervals. Facilitate C-suite and even CEO-level connectivity for our largest partners as appropriate, making sure that BlackRock’s top leaders and the vendor’s executives have a clear line of sight into the relationship’s status and strategic direction. You will prepare executive briefing materials and talking points, highlighting key decisions, risks, and achievements in the partnership.
  • Commercial Strategy & Financial Management: In close partnership with Global Strategic Sourcing (GSS), drive the commercial strategy for each vendor engagement. This includes overseeing contract negotiations, renewals, and any commercial escalations. aiming to achieve cost efficiencies and value-added services for BlackRock. Concurrently, work with Finance to maintain comprehensive visibility into vendor spend and budget impact. Track and forecast the annual spend for each vendor, ensure expenses align with budgets, and quantify the ROI of vendor-provided technology. investment with its key suppliers.
  • Partner with Technology Business Leads to ensure vendor solutions and roadmaps meet the specific needs of our businesses. For instance, coordinating with these leads to identify opportunities for co-innovation or influence vendor product development to better support BlackRock’s requirements. Work closely with GSS (procurement) as noted, as well as Legal, Risk (RQA & Tech Risk), and Compliance teams to navigate complex issues such as contract terms, regulatory requirements, and data security with vendors.

Team Leadership and Development: As a leader in Strategic Tech, you will mentor and manage junior team members dedicated to this program. Provide direction and coaching to ensure the team executes effectively on coverage models, analytics, and day-to-day vendor interactions. You will also play a role in the build-out of this new function, helping to refine organizational roles, recruit talent, and define success metrics.


Leadership Competencies:


  • Strategic Vision & Innovation: Envisions how each vendor can contribute to BlackRock’s strategy and pushes for innovative collaboration. Not satisfied with simply managing contracts, you strive to transform vendor relationships into strategic alliances that drive mutual innovation and value.
  • Collaboration & Influencing: Navigates a complex organizational landscape with ease, bringing together colleagues from different departments to solve problems and capitalize on opportunities. You can influence without formal authority and are adept at gaining buy-in for new concepts or approaches.
  • Executive Communication & Presence: Interacts confidently with senior leaders. Can represent BlackRock in high-stakes meetings with vendor CEOs or senior officials, projecting credibility and a partnership mindset. Equally, can communicate tough messages or negotiate hard when needed, maintaining professionalism and constructive tone.

Holds vendors – and yourself – accountable to high performance standards. Uses a data-driven approach to identify issues early and guide decision-making.

About this role

Role Overview
This role sits within Treasury Operations and is responsible for supporting the timely, accurate and controlled execution of payment-related activity across
BlackRock’s private markets platform. The successful candidate will play a key role in protecting client outcomes, maintaining a strong control environment
and actively managing relationships with key stakeholders across Liquidity Management, Fund Accounting, Investor Services, Tax, Business Integrity and
regional operations teams. The role also requires effective team coordination, day-to-day guidance of junior colleagues and the ability to drive
accountability, prioritisation and consistent execution across the payment oversight workflow.
The role requires strong judgement, attention to detail and a disciplined risk mindset. The candidate will be expected to operate effectively in a high-volume
environment, apply BlackRock’s control standards consistently and contribute to scalable process improvement as the business continues to grow.
The Impact
Treasury Operations plays a critical role in safeguarding client assets and supporting the delivery of BlackRock’s fiduciary responsibilities. Payment
accuracy, timeliness and control execution are central to maintaining client trust, protecting BlackRock’s reputation and ensuring obligations are met in line
with fund, investor and regulatory requirements.
The candidate will help ensure payment activity is reviewed, evidenced, escalated and completed to a high standard, while proactively managing stakeholder
engagement with Liquidity Management, Fund Accounting, Investor Services, Tax, Business Integrity and regional operations teams to support end-to-end
delivery, issue resolution and clear operational ownership.
Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee and review payment activity across GP, LP, fund expense, facility, tax, transfer and liquidity-related payment types, ensuring all required checks are completed accurately and on time.
  • Apply a strong control framework to payment review, including validation of beneficiary details, account information, payment amounts, value dates, supporting documentation and approval evidence.
  • Ensure exceptions, breaks and control issues are identified promptly, escalated appropriately and resolved with clear ownership and audit-ready evidence.
  • Act as a key stakeholder management point across Liquidity Management, Fund Accounting, Investor Services, Tax, Business Integrity and regional operations teams, ensuring priorities, dependencies, escalations and hand-offs are clearly understood and managed.
  • Review and support fund approval memos, liquidity management files, tax settlements and regional payment workflows in line with agreed procedures and service standards.
  • Support the production and enhancement of management information, client reporting and internal KPI / SLA tracking to provide transparency over volumes, quality, timeliness and control outcomes.
  • Identify process, control and workflow improvement opportunities, supporting business cases for automation, standardization and scalable operating model enhancements.
  • Maintain operating procedures and key operating processes so they remain accurate, current and aligned to the control environment.
  • Contribute to audit, governance and oversight requests by ensuring evidence is complete, organized and aligned to operating expectations.
  • Provide day-to-day team management, guidance, coaching and supervision to junior colleagues, including workflow allocation, prioritization, qualityreview, performance feedback and promotion of accountability and consistent execution across the team.

Skills and Experience

  • Experience in Treasury Operations, payments, fund operations or a comparable financial services control environment (3+ years)
  • Prior experience reviewing or approving payment instructions, ideally across multiple payment types, currencies, banking platforms and regions.
  • Strong understanding of operational risk, control execution, exception management, escalation and audit evidence standards.
  • Private markets, private equity, fund administration or alternatives experience is desirable.
  • Working knowledge of accounting principles, banking platforms, workflow tools and operational procedures.
  • Strong Excel capability, including experience working with large datasets, pivot tables, lookups and reconciliatory analysis.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting, supervising or coordinating junior team members, including coaching, work allocation, workflow prioritization, quality review and performance development.
  • Excellent organizational, analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence priorities, manage expectations and maintain effective partnerships across functions, regions and seniority levels.
  • Degree-level education or equivalent professional experience.

Candidate Profile

  • Demonstrates ownership, accountability and sound judgement in a deadline-driven environment.
  • Maintains a strong risk and control mindset, with high attention to detail and a commitment to quality.
  • Builds and manages effective stakeholder relationships across teams, regions and functions, using clear communication, ownership and follow-through to deliver strong client and business outcomes.
  • Communicates clearly and professionally, including when escalating issues or explaining complex operational matters.
  • Demonstrates effective team management behaviors, including coaching, prioritizing workloads, supporting colleague development and creating a culture of quality, accountability and controlled execution.
  • Adapts quickly to new processes, systems and priorities while maintaining operational discipline.
  • Shows curiosity and a continuous improvement mindset, with a willingness to challenge existing processes and support scalable change.
