PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns.

Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking. We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients.

Position Description

The Fund Treasurer's Office (FTO) is responsible for the governance, financial oversight, regulatory reporting, fund finance, and operational stewardship of PIMCO's public funds platform. The team partners closely with Fund Accounting, Legal, Operations, Technology, and external service providers to support the effective management of mutual funds, ETFs, and other registered investment vehicles. Key areas of focus include fund governance, financial reporting, regulatory reporting, controls, fund finance, and strategic operational initiatives.

We are seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and solutions-oriented finance professional to join the Fund Treasurer's Office and lead fund expense administration and reimbursement processing across PIMCO's public funds platform.

The immediate focus of the role will be driving backlog remediation, invoice processing, expense administration, and reimbursement activities across the platform while establishing a sustainable operating model for ongoing fund expense management. Success in this role requires strong judgment, attention to detail, and the ability to interpret fund governing documents, legal agreements, and investment guidelines to determine the appropriate treatment and allocation of expenses across a wide range of investment vehicles.

The individual will partner closely with Legal, Accounting, Fund Treasury Operations, Alternatives Operations, Technology, and external service providers to resolve complex expense, accounting, and reimbursement matters while helping modernize fund expense management through process improvements, automation, and AI-enabled solutions.

While highly operational at first, the role requires significant judgment in evaluating expense eligibility, allocation methodology, reimbursement treatment, and compliance with fund governing documents. This role offers a unique opportunity to gain broad exposure across public funds, private funds, and alternative investments while gaining deep knowledge of portfolio investments and finance operations. As PIMCO continues to evolve its operating model across traditional and alternative investment strategies, this position provides significant visibility and the opportunity to develop expertise across fund finance, operations, expense governance, and process transformation. Over time, the role may expand into broader fund finance, fund treasury, fund operations, or fund controller responsibilities based on business needs and individual development.

Responsibilities

Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Lead a high-impact expense remediation and reimbursement initiative representing more than $30 million in activity, while designing a more scalable, controlled, and transparent operating model for fund expense management.
  • Manage fund expense reimbursements, invoice processing, approval workflows, and payment administration, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and appropriate controls.
  • Review fund governing documents, investment guidelines, and legal agreements to determine the appropriate allocation and treatment of expenses across funds and portfolios.
  • Partner with Fund Treasury Operations, Accounting, Legal, and Alternatives Operations to resolve complex expense allocation, reimbursement, and accounting matters.
  • Oversee legal, litigation, and investment-related expense activities, including budgeting, allocation, reconciliation, reporting, and appropriate accounting treatment.
  • Develop management and board reporting related to expense activity, aging, allocation accuracy, reimbursements, and fund-level trends.
  • Document procedures, strengthen controls, and drive process improvements to enhance efficiency, transparency, and scalability
  • Ensure managed service provider roles and responsibilities are well established, consistently and accurately executed.
  • Partner with Technology teams on workflow automation, allocation tools, reporting capabilities, and AI-enabled solutions that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of fund expense management.
  • Collaborate effectively across Finance, Legal, Operations, Accounting, Technology, and external managed service providers to support a complex and evolving fund environment.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of a bachelor’s degree required.
  • 5+ years of experience in investment management, fund operations, fund expense administration, accounts payable, expense management, or a related finance function.
  • Accounting and finance experience required; investment company accounting knowledge preferred.
  • Understanding of mutual funds, investment vehicles, or fund structures required; exposure to alternative investments, hedge funds, or private funds is a plus.
  • Experience managing high-volume invoice processing, expense administration, reimbursement operations, or fund expense oversight activities.
  • Ability to read, interpret, and apply legal agreements, fund governing documents, and investment guidelines.
  • Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to manage complex, high-volume processes with accuracy.
  • Controls-minded with a track record of strengthening processes, improving accuracy, and mitigating financial risk.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical-thinking skills with the ability to exercise sound judgment in ambiguous situations.
  • Comfortable partnering with PIMCO senior leadership, fund controllers, accountants, attorneys, operations professionals, and business stakeholders on technical expense and allocation matters.
  • Technology savvy with a demonstrated ability to leverage automation, analytics, and AI-enabled tools to improve efficiency, controls, and reporting.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills.

Company Description

HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”).[i] Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets.[ii] This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally,[iii] offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.

Do you strive to implement the highest corporate governance standards? Would you like to use your know-how to make a difference day in and day out at the world's largest asset manager? Look no further! BlackRock is seeking an Associate within Fund Board Governance, based in Budapest. We know how it feels to be valued every single day and be recognized!

            

BlackRock takes a dynamic approach to alternative investments, creating investment vehicles that increasingly capitalize on evolving opportunities in fast-changing markets. We offer clients strategies designed to provide returns with low correlations to the broad equity and bond markets, including private equity, real estate equity and debt, fund of hedge funds, single-strategy hedge funds, long-only absolute return strategies, commodities and structured products.

As a Corporate Governance Authority, you will work closely with internal asset management teams and business partners to ensure communications operate effectively and to the highest standards.

 

Working as part of the EMEA Board Governance Team, you will provide global support function to the EBG teams in London, Dublin and Luxembourg servicing BlackRock’s Alternatives and UCITS fund ranges, as well as Corporate Boards. The Budapest team was built up in 2020 and assists the global team with a wide variety of tasks, ensures that all applicable governance requirements are met and that standard company secretarial activities are completed in a timely and effective manner. EBG team members are fundamental to the preparation of board packs and follow ups post board meetings. Excellent communication skills, organisational skills and attention to detail is required. 

                                                           

Due to its global reach, EBG Budapest is in prime position to align and ensure consistent practices for all processes.  The successful candidate will actively look for differences in processes across the fund ranges, propose the most effective approach and suggests standardization. The ideal candidate will also have ideas on automatization, how to make the transitioned processes more efficient by enhancing any kind of technological solutions. EBG team members are fundamental to the preparation of board packs and follow ups post board meetings.               

 

Responsibilities may include:

•       Preparation of board meeting documents / creation of the „board pack”

•       Agenda

•       Notice

•       Board pack

•       Meeting minutes / skeleton minutes

•       RCS filings – regulatory filings

•       Preparation of the yearly board calendar

•       Board evaluations – presentation summary

•       Applying e-signatures to documents

•       Diligent access review (board management software)

•       Collation of board statistics

•       Maintaining and updating board biographies

•       Global trackers

•       Review of minutes prepared by external service providers

•       Splitting of minutes

•       BluePrint updates

•       Director / Manager changes

•       Onboarding process – Market opening

•       Fund document in house transition

•       CBI ONR Filings

•       Document filings

•       Other ad-hoc and administrative tasks

                                                                                                                       

Successful candidates can maintain the confidence of the Boards and Committees and are likely to have worked in the investment/funds management industry, have a good knowledge of investment management.  Key personal attributes will also include a high level of intellectual agility and creativity, ability to work independently as well as part of a team and to manage business expectations. As the successful candidate will be part of a team based in London, Dublin or Luxembourg, the ability to maintain relationships and communicate remotely is of paramount importance.  

 

The role offers an excellent opportunity to develop your experience within a successful global team that has extended its footprint to Budapest.


Skills and qualifications:

• Fluent/ high level of English

• Bachelor’s degree in economics / finance or law or administration

• Experience at a multinational company, especially in financial industry is an advantage

• Excellent communication skills

• Ability to work autonomously on own tasks, whilst working in a team environment

• Ability to work under pressure with flexibility to adapt to shifting time expectations

• Highly organized and with excellent personal time management

• Attention to detail and proofing skills are essential

• Excellent relationship building and stakeholder management skills

• Strong excel skills are an advantage for the automatization purposes

• KYC / Client onboarding experience is an advantage

• Familiarity and experience with Blueprint / Diligent Software is an advantage



The salary range for Hungary is 11200000 - 16400000 HUF

  • Review business and technical requirements to create comprehensive test cases and test plans.

About the Team​

The Alternatives Client Platform (ACP) is BlackRock's global engine for client experience across our $350B+ Private Markets business, spanning Hedge Funds, Real Estate, Private Equity, Multi-Alternatives, and Infrastructure. Operating across six offices—Atlanta, New York, Seattle, Edinburgh, Hong Kong, and Mumbai—ACP delivers a unified, scalable service model that powers investor reporting, investor inquiries, and fundraising support for one of the firm's fastest-growing platforms.

ACP partners closely with investment teams, product specialists, and operations partners around the world to transform complex investment and fund data into high-quality client deliverables. Through a combination of deep product expertise, global coordination, and a strong focus on innovation—including the use of data and AI to scale our capabilities—ACP is shaping the future of how alternatives content is produced and delivered to clients.

Position overview:

We are seeking a Vice President to join the Alternatives Client Platform, supporting Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP)—BlackRock's infrastructure investment platform and one of the world's leading independent infrastructure investors. Reporting locally to the Head of ACP Asia-Pacific, this role will focus on supporting GIP's growing client base across Japan and the broader APAC region, partnering with investment, product, and client teams to deliver high-quality content production, investor reporting, and fundraising support tailored to local client needs.

This is an opportunity to operate at the intersection of investments, client experience, and technology—helping scale a recently integrated, high-growth business in one of GIP's most strategically important regions, while building deep expertise in infrastructure as an asset class.

Key Responsibilities:

Client Servicing

  • Serve as the trusted point of contact connecting BlackRock teams around the globe—including Product Strategy, Capital Formation, and Private Markets Operations—to support clients throughout their Alternatives journey, from pre-win activities (such as due diligence and RFPs) through ongoing servicing.

  • Partner with Client Experience Management ("CEM") and Client Business teams to deliver exceptional and consistent service for clients investing in Alternatives funds, driving transparency and execution in all client interactions.

  • Collaborate with internal teams to resolve operational issues and continuously enhance the client experience.

Content Production & Client Presentation

  • Operate as a subject matter expert on client reporting for Alternatives portfolios, including production of quarterly reporting deliverables, portfolio updates, and bespoke client-requested reports, with translation of materials from English to Japanese as required.

  • Prepare and deliver client-facing presentations as needed, including portfolio updates and performance reviews, presenting directly to clients in Japanese alongside Product Strategy and Client Business partners.

  • Evaluate and address reporting requirements across APAC jurisdictions, including the development of regulatory reporting frameworks to meet local compliance needs.

  • Leverage APAC-specific knowledge to partner with global support teams on the implementation of new strategies and pipeline products, ensuring seamless delivery to clients.

Scale, Innovation & Process Excellence

  • Implement best practices and process enhancements to streamline bespoke client requests and improve delivery efficiency.

  • Partner with technology and data teams to embed AI and automation into the operating model—improving data collection, reporting output, and client experience at scale.

  • Contribute to global initiatives that standardize delivery while accommodating regional, language, and regulatory nuances

Qualifications:

  • Five or more (5+) years of direct experience in private markets within an asset management or institutional allocator organization, and seven or more (7+) years of overall financial services experience.

  • Infrastructure debt or equity experience preferred.

  • Detailed knowledge of closed-end, LP drawdown fund structures and how those fund structures operate.

  • Familiarity with common private fund legal documents, including PPMs, LPAs, subscription documents, and side letter agreements.

  • Proven understanding of key performance and risk metrics used to measure private fund performance.

  • Working knowledge of the APAC private markets regulatory landscape, including jurisdiction-specific reporting and disclosure requirements.

  • Proven track record of collaborating across internal stakeholders—regionally and globally—including investment, product, and client-facing teams.

  • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to articulate sophisticated concepts, ideas, and processes clearly to both internal and external audiences.

  • Experience with data coordination, analysis, and aggregation to support client deliverables and bespoke inquiries, with meticulous attention to detail.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders in parallel, consistently delivering high-quality insights and outputs in a fast-paced environment.

  • High proficiency in Excel, including complex formulas and data manipulation to support client inquiries and reporting deliverables.

  • Strong proficiency in Word and PowerPoint, with the ability to create clear, client-ready visuals and presentations.

  • Analytical mindset with the ability to synthesize information, identify key issues, and summarize insights for senior stakeholders.

  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Japanese required.

Managing Director, Public Policy

 

About this role

BlackRock has a long history of service as a trusted, expert resource to governments and policymakers around the world. Since the Government Affairs & Public Policy (GAPP) team was created in 2009, it has steadily grown, transformed, and established BlackRock as a respected advocate for investors and the millions of retirees we serve. In recent years, that work has extended to long-term challenges such as the retirement crisis, energy security, and investment in critical infrastructure.

 

This role is for a Managing Director on GAPP to co-lead BlackRock’s legislative advocacy at the federal level in the US. This individual will be responsible for developing, prioritizing, tracking, and communicating BlackRock’s public policy priorities with Congress and the White House.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Advance BlackRock’s US federal public policy priorities, collaborating closely with Legal & Compliance, Communications, and other teams across BlackRock to ensure alignment of views.
  • Lead engagement with federal policymakers, trade associations, and clients on BlackRock’s priority issues.
  • Review key legislation and regulation and provide technical recommendations.
  • Coordinate with global public policy colleagues to ensure a consistent approach across regions.
  • Engage internal stakeholders to understand the interests of BlackRock and our clients as they relate to public policy developments; enlist subject matter experts as appropriate; assist with the development and management of internal working groups.
  • Develop and review materials for engagement with policymakers.
  • Build and maintain relationships with key policymakers and staff.
     

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; J.D. from a nationally recognized law school preferred
  • 10+ years of work experience in government relations, financial policy, or financial regulation.
  • Excellent judgment and impeccable ethics; desire to succeed in a collaborative, demanding, innovative, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Exceptional political acumen, thorough understanding of federal public policy and ability to be represent BlackRock with all policy makers. 
  • Excellent communication skills, both oral and written. Must be able to present complex concepts in a concise and understandable way.
  • Strong skills in PowerPoint, Excel, and Word.
  • Strong research and writing skills; strategic and creative thinking aptitude.
  • Exceptional organizational skills and keen attention to detail.

HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Pre-training, post-training, or novel model architecture research
Distributed training and large-scale GPU workloads
Quantitative research, financial markets, or high-frequency data
CUDA, Triton, custom kernels, or ML performance optimization
Agent-assisted or automated research methodologies

Overview

We are looking for a GPU Performance Engineer to build highly optimized CUDA kernels for low-latency inference. This role is focused on workloads where off-the-shelf runtimes and vendor libraries do not fully exploit the structure of the model, and where custom kernels, memory layouts, and execution strategies can deliver meaningful gains.

 

You will work closely with quantitative researchers and engineers to understand model structure, identify computational bottlenecks, and turn mathematical ideas into production-grade GPU implementations. You will use your understanding of GPU hardware to help shape models that are both mathematically effective and efficient to run. The problems span compact neural networks, tree-based models, and other structured inference workloads where latency, throughput, and efficiency all matter.

 

This role is a strong fit for someone who enjoys low-level optimization, performance analysis, and translating abstract models into hardware-efficient code.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, implement, and optimize custom CUDA kernels for latency-critical inference workloads
  • Develop fine-grained GPU implementations tailored to specific model structures
  • Analyze quantitative research models and computational bottlenecks to identify opportunities for parallelization and hardware-efficient execution
  • Collaborate directly with quantitative researchers to translate mathematical models into high-performance compute pipelines
  • Optimize end-to-end inference performance through kernel tuning, memory-layout design, execution strategy, I/O optimization, and precision tradeoffs
  • Profile and benchmark GPU performance
  • Improve latency and throughput in production inference systems
  • Contribute to GPU architecture decisions and performance best practices

 

What you can expect from us

 

Real Impact: By integrating sophisticated coding techniques with innovative engineering ideas, we design and optimize systems that can process massive amounts of data while still ensuring high performance and stability. You’ll see how your contributions towards developing and supporting leading-edge hardware and software technologies make a firm-wide impact that makes us all smarter, faster, and better.

 

Collaboration: You will partner closely with our Infrastructure and Strategy Developer Teams to deliver and manage scalable and highly performant systems to support trading in the region and globally.

 

Growth: For many of our roles, we don’t expect you to have prior industry experience in proprietary trading or financial services to succeed at Susquehanna. We’re looking for people who are naturally curious, relentless problem solvers, and have the desire to continuously innovate, learn, and grow.

 

Benefits: Susquehanna offers a wide array of competitive employee perks & benefits


What we're looking for

 

  • Strong proficiency in writing and optimizing CUDA kernels
  • Solid programming experience in C/C++ (preferred)
  • Deep understanding of GPU architecture, including memory hierarchy, SIMT execution, occupancy, and latency/throughput tradeoffs
  • Ability to reason about numerical stability, precision, performance tradeoffs, and how model design choices affect hardware efficiency
  • Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working with low-level systems

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, or related quantitative field
  • Strong background in linear algebra, probability, numerical methods, or scientific computing
  • Experience working with quantitative research teams or financial models
  • Demonstrated ability to improve real-world inference performance beyond baseline framework or library implementations
  • Familiarity with PTX-level behavior, tensor core utilization, or architecture-specific tuning
  • Exposure to ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, Triton, TVM, or similar systems
  • Exposure to:
    • Neural Networks
    • Tree-based models (e.g. KightGBM)
    • State space models (e.g. Mamba architectures)
  • Experience with kernel fusion, custom operators, model compilation, or graph-level optimization

This executive will play a leadership role in the next phase of digital transformation of PIMCO’s marketing capabilities. The role includes architecting data, technology, analytics and operating models that allow marketing teams to understand audiences, make better decisions, deliver more relevant experiences and measure commercial impact across institutional, wealth and intermediary channels.

A central mandate is to evolve marketing toward an AI-first approach. The leader will turn advances in artificial intelligence into governed, practical workflows for insight generation, decisioning, targeted content creation and optimization. Success requires close partnership with Marketing, Product Strategy Group, distribution teams, Technology, Legal and Compliance, and a disciplined ability to move from pilots to scaled adoption. The role is also responsible for ensuring that data, AI, personalization and marketing capabilities are designed and operated in alignment with global privacy, consent management and regulatory requirements, including GDPR and related data protection standards.

Data, Segmentation and Decision Intelligence

  • Lead customer data transformation in Marketing, partnering with Technology and other critical business stakeholders
  • Aggregate and connect first-party engagement, account, product, campaign and relevant external data into reliable, permission-aware audience and account views.
  • Build segmentation and insight capabilities that reveal client needs, buying groups, journey stages, intent signals and opportunities for acquisition, retention and cross-sell.
  • Develop propensity models, scoring and next-best-action approaches; validate performance, monitor drift and make recommendations usable by marketers and distribution channels.
  • Create decision intelligence tools that translate data into choices about audiences, channels, content, timing and investment.

AI, Personalization and Content

  • Identify, test and scale AI applications across research synthesis, insight generation, campaign planning, content production, experimentation and performance analysis.
  • Enable dynamic content assembly and personalization across web, email and other channels, with human oversight, approved source material and appropriate review controls.
  • Advance precise audience and account targeting using consented data, intent and behavioral signals, while setting standards for privacy, model governance and brand integrity.

Measurement, Optimization and ROI

  • Create a consistent measurement framework connecting reach, engagement and conversion to qualified opportunities, client activity, asset flows and retention where attribution is supportable.
  • Leverage and evolve existing ecosystem of dashboards and analytic methods for incrementality, attribution, marketing mix and return on investment; state assumptions and measurement limits clearly.
  • Use test results and performance signals to optimize targeting, creative, channel mix, journeys and marketing spend on an ongoing basis.

Leadership, Adoption and Governance

  • Provide strategic influence across marketing technology, data science, analytics, digital experience, and marketing operations, partnering with functional leaders to align capabilities, priorities, and outcomes.
  • Create practical adoption plans, training and service models so regional and channel marketing teams can use new capabilities effectively.
  • Partner with Technology, Information Security, Privacy, Legal and Compliance to establish controls for client data, AI outputs, recordkeeping, access and regulated marketing approvals.
  • Manage technology vendors, implementation partners, budgets and delivery milestones; communicate progress and tradeoffs in business terms to senior leadership.

Qualifications

  • 15 or more years of experience in marketing technology, digital transformation, data and analytics or related functions, including significant leadership of enterprise-scale programs and teams.
  • Demonstrated delivery of integrated marketing data and technology capabilities, from architecture and implementation through adoption, optimization and measurable outcomes.
  • Strong command of customer data architecture, identity resolution, data quality, consent management, APIs and integration of CRM, web, marketing automation and analytics systems.
  • Applied experience with segmentation, predictive modeling, propensity scoring, experimentation, causal measurement and ROI analytics; able to assess model quality and explain limitations.

  • Ability to translate complex technology and analytic concepts into a prioritized business roadmap and to influence senior Marketing, Product, Distribution and Technology stakeholders.

  • Experience using marketing automation platforms, such as Adobe Marketo Engage, Eloqua, Salesforce Marketing Cloud or HubSpot to execute, optimize, and measure digital marketing programs.
  • Deep understanding of GDPR and related privacy regulations, with experience establishing governance frameworks, mitigating compliance risks, and enabling responsible use of customer data across marketing programs.
  • Proven record of leading multidisciplinary teams, managing vendors and budgets, and delivering change across a global matrix.
  • Bachelor’s degree required in a relevant discipline; advanced degree in business, analytics, computer science or a related field preferred.

Position Description

We are seeking an experienced Vice President, Alternatives Accounting Manager – Income & Yield Forecasting (VP, Alts AM) to join PIMCO's Accounting and Yield Services (PAY) Group. This team is responsible for operating PIMCO's proprietary income and yield forecasting platform (PAY), which provides forward-looking income forecasting, accounting analysis, and decision-support insights across a broad range of investment products and strategies. PAY is used by the Executive Office, Portfolio Managers, Product Strategists, Fund Management, and other senior stakeholders to evaluate expected income, yield, distributions, and related outcomes, helping to inform portfolio positioning, distribution planning, risk assessment, and strategic business decisions.

The VP, Alts AM will play a key role in expanding analytical and forecasting capabilities across PIMCO's alternatives platform. In addition to supporting existing forecasting processes, the successful candidate will help develop, refine, and scale forecasting methodologies for increasingly complex alternative investment products and fund structures.

This is a highly visible and hands-on role at the intersection of investments, accounting, forecasting, and analytics. The successful candidate will serve as a subject matter expert on alternative investment forecasting, providing analyses and insights to Portfolio Managers, Product Strategists, Executive Leadership, Boards, and other senior stakeholders. Success in the role requires a broad understanding of alternative investment strategies and a deep appreciation of how underlying investments, portfolio structures, cash flows, valuations, distributions, and investor outcomes influence forecast assumptions and results. The ideal candidate is willing to roll up their sleeves and actively engage in the work, diving into complex data, investigating anomalies, challenging assumptions, and understanding the underlying drivers behind forecast results.

The VP, Alts AM will combine strong technical accounting and alternatives investment expertise with analytical rigor, intellectual curiosity, and sound judgment. This role is as much about investigative problem-solving and decision support as it is about forecasting. We are seeking someone who enjoys research, gets to the root cause of issues, and translates complex findings into clear, actionable insights that help stakeholders make better decisions. The ability to communicate complex concepts clearly and credibly to sophisticated audiences is critical.

This is an opportunity to help build and scale a growing capability supporting some of the firm's most important alternatives initiatives while partnering directly with key stakeholders across the business. The VP, Alts AM will also play an important role in the continued evolution of PIMCO's proprietary forecasting platform and related business processes, requiring close collaboration with technology teams, data providers, and business partners. This role offers the opportunity to develop deep expertise across a broad range of alternative investment products and strategies, help shape a critical forecasting function, and directly influence investment and business decisions across the firm.

Note: For recruitment purposes, this role may be referenced externally as Vice President, Alternatives Accounting Manager – Income & Yield Forecasting (PAY Group). Internally, the role is aligned to the Vice President, PAY Manager job profile.

Responsibilities

Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Manage the oversight and administration of PIMCO's proprietary income and yield forecasting platform (PAY), with a primary focus on alternative investment strategies.
  • Lead the continued expansion of forecasting capabilities across PIMCO's alternatives platform, including the development and enhancement of methodologies for new investment strategies, products, and fund structures.
  • Analyze forecast drivers at the fund, sector, asset class, and security levels to identify risks, opportunities, trends, and implications for investment and business decisions; investigate anomalies and forecast-versus-actual variances to improve forecast accuracy and reliability.
  • Assess the impact of investment activity, portfolio positioning, market events, accounting outcomes, and other business initiatives on future income and yield expectations.

Job Overview


Join our Cyber Security team as an experienced Application Security Engineer, where you’ll play a key role in driving and advancing application security in close alignment with our vulnerability management initiatives. In this senior technical position, you’ll collaborate with development, DevOps, cloud, infrastructure, and product teams to embed security controls throughout the software development lifecycle and CI/CD pipelines.

Your responsibilities will include developing and refining secure development standards, strengthening pipeline security, automating vulnerability discovery and testing, and building scalable processes for effective risk remediation. You’ll help guide vulnerability management priorities, deliver meaningful reporting and measurement of security risks, and provide actionable guidance and training to engineering teams, all with a focus on continuous improvement of our overall security posture.


Responsibilities


  • Manage and enhance pipeline security posture by building a modern DevSecOps ecosystem that leverages innovative workflows and vulnerability management to drive effective, scalable security throughout the development lifecycle.
  • Modernize vulnerability management by integrating AI-driven analysis that correlates technical risks with business impact, enabling more informed prioritization and remediation.
  • Explore and implement the responsible use of AI to improve vulnerability discovery, code review, threat modeling, risk prioritization, security monitoring, and remediation recommendations.
  • Lead threat modeling and security reviews for AI-enabled systems, including risks such as prompt injection, insecure model output handling, sensitive data disclosure, model abuse, excessive agency, and data or model poisoning.
  • Define metrics and reporting that communicate the security posture and risk exposure of AI-enabled applications to technical teams and senior leadership.
  • Define and maintain secure SDLC policies, procedures, and workflows—and translate these into actionable technical requirements.
  • Drive security controls in CI/CD pipelines (SAST, DAST, SCA, secret detection, container scanning, API testing, etc.).
  • Work directly with development teams to explain findings, risks, and remediation steps, guiding vulnerability remediation based on an internal risk matrix of attack vectors and business objectives.
  • Advance software supply chain security, including dependency governance, artifact integrity, SBOM adoption, and third-party risk management.
  • Enhance software development pipelines with automated vulnerability and risk measurement, implementing promotion guardrails that balance effective risk management with delivery speed.
  • Support incident response for application and pipeline security events.

Qualifications


  • Ability to leverage frontier AI models to enhance secure code scanning, vulnerability discovery, and application penetration testing.
  • Experience in application security, DevSecOps, secure SDLC, vulnerability management, or security engineering.
  • Experience building advanced dashboards that highlight key risk indicators, trends, and actionable insights for technical and business stakeholders.
  • Hands-on experience collaborating with developers to remediate vulnerabilities.
  • Proficiency with CI/CD platforms and source control tools (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Jenkins, etc.).
  • Use of application security testing tools (SAST, DAST, SCA, container scanning, API testing, etc.).
  • Experience conducting security reviews of application architectures and APIs to identify design weaknesses, vulnerabilities, and potential attack paths.
  • Familiarity with modern architectures (microservices, containers, APIs, cloud-native apps).
  • Programming/scripting experience (Python, PowerShell, Bash, C#, Java, JS/TS, Ruby, etc.).
  • Working knowledge of AWS/Azure cloud security concepts.
  • Experience developing technical documentation and secure coding guides.
  • Effective communication of technical security concepts.
  • Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to influence secure development practices and drive adoption.
  • Demonstrated adaptability and the ability to pivot strategy or priorities when faced with significant technical challenges or evolving project scopes.
  • Risk-based mindset with attention to business and delivery needs.
  • Initiative and independent leadership with strong project management.
  • Analytical and detail-oriented; excellent problem solving.
  • Thrives in fast-paced, multi-team environments.
  • Metrics-driven approach to program effectiveness.
  • Clear written and verbal communication of vulnerabilities and remediation.
  • Passion for enabling secure development through automation, training, and scalable processes.
  • Familiarity with frameworks/standards (NIST, CIS, ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS).
  • Some knowledge of application security risks and frameworks (OWASP Top 10, CWE/SANS 25, secure coding, threat modeling).
  • Experience leading or maturing application security/DevSecOps programs is a plus.
  • Developer-first tools and integration (pull requests, issue tracking, IDEs) is preferred.
  • Software supply chain security (SBOM, dependency governance, artifact signing) is a plus.
  • Threat modeling methodologies (STRIDE, attack trees, agile models).
  • Experience with containers and cloud-native platforms (Docker, Kubernetes, ECS/EKS/AKS/OpenShift) desired.
  • Experience providing application security and secure coding training is an added value.
  • Relevant certifications (CSSLP, CISSP, GWAPT, GWEB, OSWE, AWS/Azure Security) are an asset.

About Us:
Founded 20 years ago and headquartered in Chicago, the DV Group of financial services firms has grown to more than 600 people operating throughout North America, Europe and Asia. Since spinning out of a large brokerage firm in 2016, DV Trading has rapidly scaled as an independent proprietary trading firm utilizing its own capital, trading strategies, and risk management methodologies to provide liquidity to worldwide financial markets and hedging opportunities to commodity producers and users. Now, DV group affiliates include two broker dealers, a cryptocurrency market making firm, and a bourgeoning investment adviser.

Overview:
We are seeking a full-stack developer to join our risk team. This role supports the design, build, and operation of the in-house risk engine, which powers real-time calculation and monitoring of PnL, VaR, greeks, risk slides, and other key risk metrics.

The ideal candidate combines solid backend and frontend development skills with strong DevOps fundamentals and hands-on experience using AI tooling in day-to-day development. You will work closely with senior risk developers, quantitative analysts, and market risk analysts to turn financial models into reliable, production-ready applications and keep them running smoothly under live trading conditions.

Job Responsibilities:
- Build and maintain real-time risk systems used daily by risk, traders, and executives, including:
  - 24/5 live PnL tracking
  - VaR and other exposure calculations
  - Web-based risk dashboards
  - Interactive analytical tools
  - Alerting and monitoring systems
- Own deployment, CI/CD, and infrastructure for risk applications: containerization, pipeline automation, environment management, observability, and incident response.
- Improve system reliability, performance, and availability, with a focus on low latency and stability during market hours.
- Use AI-assisted development tools (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) to accelerate development, testing, documentation, and debugging.
- Develop and enhance applications that integrate LLM APIs for automation, analysis, and workflow improvements.
- Build responsive front-end interfaces for visualizing and interacting with risk metrics.
- Collaborate with the risk team to understand requirements and implement risk models.
- Write clean, well-documented, and tested code; participate in code reviews and design discussions.

Requirements:
- 4+ years of professional experience as a full-stack developer, preferably in the financial industry or proprietary trading.
- Strong proficiency in Python for data processing, backend logic, and model integration.
- Solid DevOps experience: Docker, CI/CD pipelines (e.g. GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins), Linux administration, and monitoring/logging tools (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana). Experience with Kubernetes or infrastructure-as-code (e.g. Terraform, Ansible) is a plus.
- Hands-on experience with AI coding assistants and agentic development workflows, and a practical understanding of how to apply them effectively and safely.
- Experience integrating LLM APIs (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic) into applications, including prompt design, tool/function calling, and evaluation.
- Experience with at least one modern JavaScript framework (React, Angular, or Vue).
- Proficiency in SQL and a solid understanding of relational databases (e.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL) and/or NoSQL stores (e.g. Redis).
- Understanding of data structures, APIs, and real-time data processing.
- Familiarity with real-time data visualization.
- Exposure to quantitative models or working with quants is a plus.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Benefits:
- Discretionary bonus eligibility
- Medical, dental, and vision insurance
- HSA, FSA, and Dependent Care Options
- Employer Paid Group Term Life and AD&D insurance
- Voluntary LTD, Life & AD&D insurance
- Flexible Vacation policy
- Retirement plan with employer match

All resumes submitted by search firms to DV via e-mail, the Internet, personal delivery, facsimile, or any other method without a valid written agreement shall be deemed the sole property of DV, and no fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by DV. DV is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

About Bridgewater   
Bridgewater Associates is a premier asset management firm, focused on delivering unique insight and partnership for the most sophisticated global institutional investors.   
Our investment process is driven by a tireless pursuit to understand how the world’s markets and economies work — using cutting edge technology to validate and execute on timeless and universal investment principles.   
Founded in 1975, we are a community of independent thinkers who share a commitment for excellence. By fostering a culture of openness, transparency, and inclusion, we strive to unlock the most complex questions in investment strategy, management, and corporate culture.   
Explore more information about Bridgewater on our website here.  
Our Culture  
Our culture is anchored in excellence, meaning constant improvement, and it is deeply tied to our mission. Because markets are objective, competitive, and getting smarter everyday, we need to keep rapidly improving to have any chance of beating them. Truth is our most essential tool for engaging with the markets and constantly improving because once you know what's true about your problems and opportunities, you can determine how to get better. Valuing truth means being transparent about your decision-making and mistakes, giving and receiving feedback with humility, and fighting for the best answers over hierarchy, ego, or self-interest. Operating this way is hard – it's only possible because we build meaning in our work and relationships. This meaning comes from the audacity of the mission, and the joy of working alongside people who make you a better version of yourself. The culture, like Bridgewater itself, is always evolving. In 1997 our founder Ray Dalio wrote down his lessons, starting with a Philosophy Statement which remains our foundation. This later evolved into a set of 300+ Principles. In 2022, when Ray transitioned the company, we re-underwrote several of those principles and evolved others, with a specific focus on Meritocracy. Today the culture sits, alongside our people, as our most important edge. When we get it right, it’s the engine that powers everything else.  
Explore more information about Bridgewater’s culture on our website here.  
Finance Department
Finance leads Bridgewater’s financial strategy and serves as a strategic advisor to businesses across the firm. We partner with leaders to translate strategy into financially sound plans, evaluate growth opportunities, and make informed decisions about how to allocate capital. Our work builds financial resilience and drives long-term shareholder value, supported by rigorous analysis, reporting, and controls. We are also transforming how Finance operates, using AI and automation to deliver faster insights and focus more of our expertise on the decisions that shape the firm’s future. 
About the role
Finance Associates are core members of the department from day one. You will partner with leaders across the firm, build the analysis behind important decisions, and communicate the “so what” behind the numbers. Finance Associates work across areas such as business planning and analysis, corporate finance, and investor relations, gaining a broad view of how Bridgewater operates. 
Every Finance Associate joins the Finance Associate Program, which helps early-career finance professionals develop, grow, and connect within Bridgewater’s Finance organization. The program has three pillars: 

Training and professional development: Training in AI, finance fundamentals, advanced Excel, and financial modeling, with a path tailored to your role. 
Mentorship and exposure to leadership: A one-on-one mentor from among Finance’s senior professionals with opportunities to learn from leaders across the organization. 
Community and cohort engagement: Join a cohort of FAs across Finance who come together to exchange ideas, learn from one another, and build relationships through discussions and events they help organize. 

What You Will Do 

Build financial models and analyses that inform leadership decisions and translate insights into clear recommendations. 
Drive critical processes including planning and budgeting, financial reporting, capital planning, valuation, and liquidity analysis. 
Partner with business leaders to pressure-test decisions before resources are committed. 
Use AI tools and automation to make Finance’s work faster, more accurate, and more scalable. 
Prepare concise materials and narratives for senior leadership. 

You Will Be A Fit For The Role If You Are 

Analytical: Detail-oriented and able to turn numbers into a story, separating the big from the small. 
AI-minded: Energized by using AI to redefine what finance can do, with hands-on curiosity about AI tools and large language models. 
An owner: Proactive and gritty, with the drive to carry work from idea through execution. 
An independent thinker: Comfortable using data and logic to challenge assumptions thoughtfully. 
A clear communicator: Able to explain complex ideas simply, ask sharp questions, and build trust with senior stakeholders. 
Feedback-oriented: Eager to seek and give feedback, and quick to learn from mistakes. 

Minimum Qualifications

This role is for graduating seniors in the Class of 2027 completing a four-year degree from an accredited undergraduate institution with an academic focus or demonstrated interest in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related field. 
A strong academic track record and demonstrated math and analytical ability. 
Evidence of leadership on or off campus. 
Proficiency in Excel and experience using AI tools to improve analysis or streamline work. 

Compensation 
The wage range for this role is $85,000 - $110,000 inclusive of base salary and discretionary target bonus. The expected base salary for this role is between 80% - 90% of this wage range. 
Physical Requirements
The anticipated onsite requirement for this role is four days per week at our New York City campus. 
Why Choose Bridgewater?  
It takes all types to make Bridgewater great. We seek a diverse group of innovative thinkers and push them to engage in rigorous and thoughtful inquiry. We develop people through an honest examination of their abilities and performance, enabling personal growth and professional development. We strive to provide you opportunities that will challenge you and unlock your potential.   
One of our core priorities at Bridgewater is to enable our employees to build a great life and career, and we believe our benefits are an important extension of that philosophy. Meet the Team
Core to the health and growth of our business, Millennium’s Information Technology organization supports a flexible, scalable technology environment powered by advanced proprietary systems and the continued development of next-generation analytical and trading capabilities. The global Network & Data Center team supports the firm’s physical infrastructure across data centers and office technology rooms, with a focus on operational reliability, connectivity, capacity management, and disciplined infrastructure operations.

What You'll Do

  • Own the data center ticket queue end to end, ensuring the timely triage, prioritization, assignment, and resolution of incidents, service requests, and change tasks across the New Jersey data center estate and New York office technology rooms
  • Serve as the accountable lead for day-to-day operational health across power, cooling, space, cabling, security, and environmental monitoring, escalating to engineering teams as appropriate
  • Lead, coach, and coordinate a team of Data Center Specialists, establishing daily priorities, managing shift coverage, and maintaining operational discipline in a 24x7 environment
  • Drive ITIL-aligned incident and change-management practices, acting as the operational bridge between the field team and Network Engineering to ensure changes are planned, reviewed, and executed safely
  • Maintain and improve operational runbooks, SOPs, and knowledge-base articles, ensuring procedures remain current, accessible, and consistently adopted
  • Own the accuracy and completeness of asset, rack, patching, and inventory records in ServiceNow and Nlyte, identifying and remediating data-quality gaps across CMDB and DCIM platforms
  • Oversee server provisioning and inventory lifecycle activities, including hardware intake, rack assignment, imaging, operating system deployment, Engineering handoff, and asset tracking through decommissioning
  • Manage vendor engagements, maintenance windows, data center facility work, and third-party smart-hands activity; monitor infrastructure capacity and health, report operational metrics to leadership, and lead process, tooling, automation, and integration improvements

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of experience in data center or large-scale infrastructure operations, including at least 3 years as a team lead, operations manager, or senior individual contributor; financial services or other mission-critical environment experience is strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to manage and prioritize high-volume operational ticket queues through ITSM platforms such as ServiceNow or Jira, with a record of driving SLA adherence and continuous improvement
  • Strong hands-on experience in data center physical operations, including racking and stacking, structured cabling, patch management, hardware lifecycle management, and installation, move, add, and change coordination
  • Solid understanding of data center power and cooling, including PDUs, UPS systems, dual feeds, N+1 and 2N redundancy concepts, capacity management, and remote-management technologies such as iDRAC, iLO, console servers, and out-of-band management
  • Experience with server provisioning workflows, including bare-metal imaging, PXE boot environments, BMC configuration, and CMDB-driven intake processes; familiarity with Ansible, Foreman, or comparable automation and provisioning platforms is a plus
  • CCNA-level networking knowledge, including TCP/IP, VLANs, trunking, subnetting, and basic routing, with the ability to coordinate and validate network cabling and connectivity activities with Engineering teams
  • Experience with DCIM, CMDB, and monitoring platforms such as Nlyte, ServiceNow, Prometheus, or comparable tools, including inventory-accuracy and data-quality practices
  • Strong leadership, documentation, communication, and organizational skills, with the ability to coordinate global teams, manage competing priorities, produce operational and capacity reporting, and contribute to automation using Python, PowerShell, or Bash

The estimated base salary range for this position is $175,000 to $250,000, which is specific to New York and may change in the future. Two Sigma is a leading quantitative investment management and trading firm. The company applies a scientific approach to investing, combining cutting-edge technology, artificial intelligence, data science, and quantitative research with rigorous human inquiry to capitalize on market opportunities and deliver alpha for investors.

Our team of engineers, quantitative researchers and data scientists looks beyond the traditional to test hypotheses and develop creative solutions to some of the world’s most complex economic problems.
We are looking for a credit analyst to join the Convertible Arbitrage team within Derivatives and Relative Value (DRV), a modeling team that aims to expand the spectrum of asset classes and strategies used for systematic investment management at Two Sigma.  Our convertible arbitrage strategy identifies mispriced convertible securities and captures the difference between market price and fair value by trading the convertible and hedging its exposures with equities, equity options, Treasury futures, corporate bonds and credit default swaps.  Our goal is to apply Two Sigma's data science and systematic trading expertise to convertible arbitrage, and this role will bring fundamental credit expertise to that effort.
You will take on the following responsibilities:

  • Conduct fundamental credit analysis on convertible issuers, including capital structure, liquidity, covenants, recovery and refinancing risk
  • Assess credit risk on positions under stress, and work with portfolio managers on sizing, hedging and exit decisions
  • Provide analytical support for primary market opportunities, including new issuance, buybacks and other capital markets transactions
  • Develop issuer-level views that support engagement with issuers and counterparties
  • Monitor credit exposures across the portfolio and flag emerging risks proactively
  • Help build data-driven tools and processes, including LLM-based and agentic workflows, that make credit analysis faster and more scalable
You should possess the following qualifications:

  • 5–10 years of experience in fundamental credit analysis, on the buy side (credit, distressed or convertible funds) or sell side (leveraged finance, high-yield or convertible research)
  • A deep understanding of corporate capital structures, credit documentation and recovery analysis
  • Familiarity with convertible bonds, or with how equity and credit interact across the capital structure; hands-on convertible experience is a strong plus
  • Proficiency using AI and agentic workflows for research and analysis (e.g., using LLM tools to process filings, transcripts and credit documents)
  • Comfort working with and analyzing data programmatically; Python or similar experience is a plus
  • Strong analytical and communication skills, and the ability to present concise, well-reasoned recommendations to portfolio managers

BlackRock's Financial Markets Advisory group (“FMA”) provides counsel to financial institutions, sovereigns and official institutions across a range of strategic, capital, balance sheet, risk and regulatory matters, across both public and private markets. At the heart of “BlackRock as a platform” FMA aims to build or deepen BlackRock’s relationships with our clients’ senior management, serving them on their most critical and most complex needs.

Career Kickstarter: Trading is an immersive five-day program at Optiver’s Amsterdam office, offering final-year students at European Universities a direct pathway to a career in trading.
Over the course of one week, you’ll build your understanding of trading through theory, realistic simulations and exposure to Optiver’s trading floor. Through a blend of interactive lectures, trading games, and expert mentorship, you’ll learn how to think and act like a trader.
If you prove to be a good match, you may receive a full-time job offer to join Optiver as a Graduate Trader once the program is complete.

Where: Optiver Amsterdam Headquarters

A week of learning, decision-making and trading in action. Throughout the program, our dedicated Trading Education Team will mentor you, providing guidance and feedback designed to sharpen your skills and accelerate your development.

Discover options theory: Develop an understanding of options theory and how it applies to trading.
Build your market judgement: Gain insight into how traders use information, probability and risk-reward trade-offs to make decisions in changing conditions.
Engage in trading games: Participate in fast-paced games that mimic real-world trading scenarios, helping sharpen your instincts and decision-making skills under pressure.

Pathway to a career: Demonstrate your potential during the program, and you may receive a direct offer to join Optiver as a Graduate Trader.

Your colleagues will include internationally recognized experts in machine learning research as well as highly experienced finance and technology professionals.   • Prepare ad-hoc special projects and tax-related requests from various investors with accuracy and timeliness

Join us for a two-day Discovery Summit designed exclusively for PhD students and postdocs curious about careers in quantitative finance. Whether you’re exploring new applications of your research or considering a transition to industry, this event offers a unique window into life as a quant. You’ll dive into topics like options theory, financial data, and machine learning while seeing how cutting-edge research connects to real-world trading. Throughout the program, you’ll meet with senior quants, participate in trading games, and explore our trading floor firsthand. From networking with junior researchers to discussions with senior quantitative researchers, you’ll gain insight into both the intellectual challenges and collaborative culture of our work. 


What we're looking for

This opportunity is for those who will be completing their PhD in 2029 in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning, Operations Research, or Economics. Please submit your resume to be considered for this program.

We will be in touch towards the end of 2026 regarding next steps for attendance.

Susquehanna is a global quantitative trading firm powered by scientific rigor, curiosity, and innovation. By uniting deep market expertise with cutting-edge technology, we excel in solving complex problems and pushing boundaries together.

Role Summary
Cloud Storage Platform Engineering provides secure, scalable, resilient, and automated storage capabilities for applications and data across the firm. The Cloud Storage Platform Principal is a senior individual contributor responsible for defining the architecture, engineering standards, automation, and operational direction for enterprise cloud storage platforms. The role brings deep expertise across NetApp, Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, Nasuni, and AWS native storage services, including Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS, Amazon S3, and backup capabilities. The Principal serves as the design authority and technical escalation point for cloud storage, helping enable CloudNext and data center exit outcomes while strengthening the skills of the broader storage team.

Responsibilities

The Principal Cloud Engineer (Storage) owns the strategy, architecture, engineering, and reliability outcomes for enterprise cloud storage platforms. The role balances strategic leadership with hands-on delivery, establishing reusable patterns and automation while partnering with infrastructure, cloud engineering and operations, application teams, architecture, security, and service owners.

  • Lead the architecture, design, and evolution of cloud storage platforms in support of CloudNext and data center exit objectives.
  • Define enterprise storage patterns across NetApp, Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, Nasuni, Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS, Amazon S3, and backup services.
  • Engineer secure, scalable, highly available, and resilient storage solutions for enterprise application and data workloads.
  • Own technical standards for performance, capacity, availability, recoverability, data protection, lifecycle management, and cost efficiency.
  • Design and implement automation for provisioning, configuration, policy enforcement, monitoring, and operational support using infrastructure-as-code and Git-based workflows.
  • Create reusable modules, reference architectures, guardrails, and self-service patterns that support consistent adoption at scale.
  • Provide technical leadership for workload discovery, storage assessment, migration planning, data movement, cutover, validation, and decommissioning activities.
  • Partner with application and platform teams to select appropriate storage services based on workload requirements, performance, resilience, security, and cost.
  • Embed monitoring, logging, alerting, capacity management, and performance analytics into cloud storage platforms.
  • Serve as the escalation point for complex storage incidents and performance issues, leading root-cause analysis and durable remediation.
  • Assess and manage dependencies across networking, identity and access, encryption, backup, operational tooling, and regulatory controls.
  • Guide the transition from traditional on-premises storage to cloud storage platforms while mentoring and upskilling storage engineers.
  • Influence roadmaps and investment decisions for cloud and on-premises storage technologies as the platform remit evolves.
  • Participate in an Agile delivery model, contributing to epics and stories, tracking work, and supporting planned releases.

Business Knowledge

  • Deep understanding of how storage availability, performance, recoverability, and data protection affect business services and client outcomes.
  • Ability to translate application requirements into fit-for-purpose storage architecture and clear technical decisions.
  • Ability to balance migration speed, platform resilience, security, operational sustainability, and financial stewardship.
  • Experience operating enterprise infrastructure in a regulated, risk-aware environment with strong security and compliance expectations.
  • Makes decisions aligned with enterprise technology strategy while improving platform stability, delivery consistency, and time to adoption.

Qualifications
Required:

  • Bachelor's degree or the equivalent combination of education and relevant experience AND typically 10+ years of experience designing, engineering, and operating enterprise storage or cloud infrastructure with senior-level impact.
  • Deep hands-on expertise with NetApp and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, with strong knowledge of Nasuni and AWS native storage services such as Amazon EFS, Amazon EBS, Amazon S3, and AWS Backup.
  • Expert knowledge of storage architecture, file and block services, data protection, replication, backup and recovery, performance engineering, capacity planning, and lifecycle management.
  • Experience designing storage solutions for highly available, resilient, secure, and large-scale enterprise workloads.
  • Strong infrastructure automation experience using tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible, scripting, APIs, and Git-based delivery workflows.
  • Working knowledge of AWS networking, identity and access management, encryption, monitoring, logging, and security controls that support storage platforms.
  • Proven ability to lead complex storage migrations and resolve performance, availability, and integration challenges across infrastructure and application layers.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence architecture decisions and explain tradeoffs to technical and business stakeholders.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and influencing teams without formal line management.

Preferred:

  • Experience in financial services — asset management, investment banking, or fintech.

About this role

We are seeking a strategic and experienced HR Risk and Operational Excellence Vice President to strengthen governance frameworks, enhance reporting mechanisms, and enable effective oversight of HR risks and operations. This role is a second-line function focused on empowering HR teams to address risks and operational challenges effectively while maintaining accountability at the appropriate levels.


The ideal candidate will have deep expertise in operational risk governance, the ability to provide actionable insights, and a collaborative approach to driving compliance and process improvement. This role does not directly remediate issues but instead establishes frameworks, guidance, and reporting mechanisms to empower teams to resolve challenges independently.


Key Responsibilities

Operational Risk Management and Governance

  • Analyze data and trends to identify emerging HR risks and prioritize mitigation strategies.
  • Define and oversee HR Business Risk Indicators (BRIs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to monitor risk and performance.
  • Advise HR leadership with actionable insights and strategic guidance on risk management and governance practices.
  • Develop and implement governance frameworks for the proactive identification, tracking, and management of HR risks.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to monitor remediation progress, ensuring accountability and ownership at the appropriate levels.
  • Prepare and deliver governance reports to senior management, summarizing key metrics, trends, and actionable insights to inform decision-making.
  • Promote transparency and adherence to governance processes across HR functions to enhance risk mitigation and compliance.

Policy Governance

  • Support and maintain the HR Policy Governance framework, ensuring it aligns with regional regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with Employment Legal and HR teams to design and enhance mechanisms for horizon scanning, enabling functions with the ability to timely identify regulatory changes that may impact HR policies.
  • Provide governance oversight to confirm policy updates are operationalized effectively by the relevant HR functions, with clear ownership and accountability.

Third-Party Governance

  • Act as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for HR third-party risk management, enabling Vendor Relationship Owners (VROs) to comply with sourcing, vendor management, privacy, and information security policy requirements.
  • Support the development and maintenance of effective third-party governance frameworks, ensuring HR vendor inventory oversight aligns with organizational standards.

Audit Readiness and Support

  • Act as a liaison between HR teams and internal/external auditors, ensuring alignment of expectations and clear communication throughout the audit lifecycle.
  • Establish and maintain an audit preparedness framework, defining protocols for ongoing monitoring and periodic reviews of HR processes to confirm readiness.
  • Coordinate with process owners across HR functions to address requests for clarification, additional evidence, or follow-up actions during audits.
  • Monitor the resolution of audit issues by tracking management responses and action plans, ensuring timely and effective remediation.
  • Conduct independent assessments of remediation actions to confirm their effectiveness and alignment with audit objectives.

Training and Development

  • Design and deliver targeted training programs to increase awareness of HR risk governance and policy requirements, including training on audit preparedness to equip HR teams with the tools and knowledge needed to navigate audit processes confidently.
  • Provide specialized coaching to HR Teams on essential systems and governance processes, supporting smooth transitions for new initiatives.

Qualifications

  • 6-8+ years of experience in HR governance, compliance, or risk management roles, preferably in a global, matrixed environment.

  • Proficiency in MS Office (Excel, PowerPoint) and familiarity with privacy and compliance programs.
  • Clear, effective communication skills, including proficiency in ‘Plain-English’ writing and visual storytelling.
  • Experience navigating ambiguity and driving initiatives independently within a dynamic environment.

About this role

Company Description

HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”.[i] Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets.[ii] This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally,[iii] offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board.

The Strategic Fund Financing team focuses on sourcing and optimizing credit facilities across the PFS platform. These include asset-backed facilities secured by HPS fund investments, subscription facilities secured by capital commitments from HPS investors, as well as more bespoke financings.
